You are in an **Archon Horizon** workspace at `.`.

Load the **`horizon`** skill FIRST. Read it at the ABSOLUTE path
`/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` (also exported as `$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`) — do NOT use a
relative path like `.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md`, which fails when your
shell starts in a member project rather than the workspace root. The skill
explains where the state lives, the tools, and this workspace's conventions
(one-shot discipline, git commits, the final report).

The installed workspace skills are stale (horizon, horizon-inbox, project-git, task-status). Do not overwrite deliberate local edits automatically, but do not ignore the drift. Until it is reconciled: use the `lean-check` LSP loop before and after Lean edits; spawn and wait for a bounded native subagent on multi-file/multi-proof work; and dispatch `janitor` (`ground` fallback) for inbox/roadmap/task health warnings and before terminal completion.

Before modifying files, inspect the required and conversational inbox lanes:
`"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --mine --status open --kind protection --json`
then `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --mine --unread --kind conversation --json`.
Protections are standing constraints even when already read. Address or explicitly
acknowledge unread conversations before ordinary advisory inbox material.

# Task
Task: ajc-albanese
Title: Albanese leg: codim-one extension, Abel-Jacobi, symmetric powers, universal property
Project(s) — work across all of them:
- Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge at MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge
References: roadmap=AJC.albanese,AJC.albanese.codim1,AJC.albanese.symmetric,AJC.albanese.universal; inbox=I-0074,I-0493

CLOSE THE ALBANESE LEG. Roadmap AJC.albanese and its three children (.codim1, .symmetric, .universal). The headline universal-property theorem is ALREADY sorry-free — what is missing is the construction layer beneath it, so this task is about supplying real inputs to a statement that already stands, not about restating anything.

THREE FRONTS, with the actual sorry sites.

 (a) CODIMENSION-ONE RATIONAL-MAP EXTENSION (AJC.albanese.codim1). Albanese/CodimOneExtension.lean: CodimOneFree (:216, :218), gammaSpecField_ringEquiv (:752), localRing_dvr_of_codim_one (:1402), indeterminacy_pure_codim_one_into_grpScheme (:1751). Finish the diagonal-intersection and function-field pullback steps showing a rational map to an abelian variety has no codimension-one indeterminacy. The blueprint frontier flags Milne Lemma 3.3 (pure-codim-1 structure of the indeterminacy locus into a group variety) as 22 unlocks / 23 uses — the highest-leverage node in this cone, and the sibling Rebuild has a whole Albanese/CodimOne* family (CodimOneMilne31, CodimOneStalkRegularity, CodimOneDVRStalk, CodimOneSmoothReduced) covering the same ground. READ THOSE FIRST.

 (b) ABEL-JACOBI AND SYMMETRIC POWERS (AJC.albanese.symmetric). Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean: abelJacobi (:335), SymmetricPower (:382), symmetricPowerAVMap (:416), symmetricPowerToJacobian (:453), descentThroughBirationalSigma (:496), albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq (:533). Six honest construction and bridge gaps: Abel-Jacobi, the symmetric-power carrier and quotient API, symmetric sums, the map to Pic0, birational descent, the factorisation connector. The characteristic-free symmetric-power route is already specified cleanly in the blueprint — follow it rather than inventing a route.

 (c) THE UNIVERSAL PROPERTY (AJC.albanese.universal). Complete descent through the birational g-th symmetric power and the factorisation biconditional. The connector now has the correct two directions: pointed rigidity plus quotient uniqueness forward, restriction along Q -> Q+(g-1)P0 backward. Two typed-sorry bridges; once they close, the existing theorem stands unconditionally.

RIGIDITY IS YOURS TOO, if it blocks you: RigidityLemma.lean has three open obligations (:481 saturated-open-to-affine, :673 dense-open, :764 rigidity_core) and pointed rigidity is a direct input to (c).

DISCIPLINE. Search before proving — horizon search spans your project, the sibling Rebuild, the standalone SubProjects/Albanese, and mathlib. The Rebuild Albanese/ directory is 24 files / 7.3k lines and its codim-one family is more developed than yours in places. Use the LSP loop between edits, lake build at session boundaries.

COORDINATION. You are one of four AJC teams. You consume Pic0 facts from ajc-pic0av (degree map, Pic0(k) = ker degree) — ask on the AJC conversation thread rather than proving them yourself or editing Picard/. Your files are Albanese/ and RigidityLemma.lean. Never edit files outside Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge.

This is a headless, one-shot session: work the task's REAL objective as far
as you genuinely can, committing progress as you go, then finish with the
brief final report the skill specifies.

1	---
2	name: horizon
3	description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
4	---
5	
6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.
19	
20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22	
23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
26	  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
27	  another team.
28	- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).
30	
31	Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
32	A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
33	commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
34	`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
35	other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
36	conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
37	redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
38	object in `horizon inbox list --json`.
39	
40	## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)
41	
42	**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
43	somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
44	written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
45	situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
46	finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.
47	
48	The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
49	project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
50	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
51	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
52	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
53	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
54	
55	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
56	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
57	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
58	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
59	  item's status current with `--status` and its strategy prose current with
60	  `--summary` / `--summary-file` (there is no `--strategy` flag). It doubles as
61	  the **project board**:
62	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
63	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
64	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
65	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
66	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
67	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
68	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
69	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
70	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
71	  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
72	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
73	  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
74	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
75	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
76	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
77	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
78	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
79	- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
80	  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
81	  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
82	  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
83	  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
84	- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
85	  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
86	  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
87	  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
88	  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
89	- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
90	  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
91	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
92	  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
93	- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
94	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
95	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
96	- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
97	  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
98	  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.
99	
100	## Your session's identity (environment variables)
101	
102	The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:
103	
104	| Variable | Meaning |
105	|---|---|
106	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
107	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
108	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
109	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
110	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
111	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
112	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
113	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
114	| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
115	| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |
116	
117	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
118	
119	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
120	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
121	
122	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
123	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
124	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
125	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
126	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
127	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
128	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
129	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
130	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
131	
132	## One-shot discipline (important)
133	
134	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
135	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
136	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
137	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
138	
139	## Pick the highest-value work
140	
141	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
142	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
143	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
144	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
145	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
146	
147	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
148	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
149	the objective is large. Leave a `"$HORIZON_BIN" task comment <task_id> --body …`
150	at each significant step. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
151	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
152	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
153	(it returns to the queue).
154	
155	## Fresh-context checkpoints
156	
157	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
158	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
159	checkpoints:
160	
161	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
162	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
163	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
164	  clean/build result.
165	
166	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
167	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
168	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
169	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
170	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
171	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
172	terminal `done` claim.
173	
174	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
175	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
176	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
177	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
178	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
179	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
180	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
181	
182	## Warnings are work
183	
184	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
185	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
186	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
187	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
188	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
189	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
190	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
191	why.
192	
193	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
194	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
195	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
196	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
197	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
198	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
199	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
200	
201	## Do the work (Lean)
202	
203	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
204	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
205	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
206	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
207	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
208	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
209	configured final build covers the same files.
210	
211	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
212	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
213	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
214	mathlib — query it:
215	
216	| You want | Use | Not |
217	|---|---|---|
218	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
219	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
220	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
221	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
222	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
223	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
224	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
225	
226	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
227	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
228	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
229	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
230	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
231	back to grep.
232	
233	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
234	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
235	
236	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
237	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
238	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
239	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
240	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
241	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
242	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
243	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
244	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
245	
246	## Read the other projects
247	
248	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
249	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
250	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
251	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
252	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
253	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
254	
255	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
256	
257	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
258	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
259	needs no permission.
260	
261	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
262	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
263	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
264	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
265	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
266	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
267	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
268	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
269	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
270	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
271	
272	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
273	
274	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
275	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
276	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
277	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
278	
279	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
280	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
281	
282	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status (`--status`) and strategy prose
283	  (`--summary`), not a re-narration of the diff.
284	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
285	  as **memory**.
286	
287	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
288	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
289	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
290	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
291	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
292	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
293	shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
294	answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
295	pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
296	
297	## Resuming after an interruption
298	
299	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
300	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
301	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
302	
303	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
304	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
305	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
306	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
307	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
308	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
309	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
310	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
311	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
312	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
313	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
314	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
315	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
316	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
317	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
318	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
319	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
320	
321	## Final report (your last message)
322	
323	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
324	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
325	Recommended sections: `## Summary`, `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
326	`## Why I stopped`, `## Next` (keep at least `## Progress` and
327	`## Why I stopped`). In `## Progress`, one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
328	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
329	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
330	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
331	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
332	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
333	not by itself a reason to stop.
334	
335	## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)
336	
337	There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
338	and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
339	workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
340	`subagents` skill):
341	
342	- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
343	- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
344	- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?

9	/-!
10	# The symmetric power is a colimit of the permutation action
11	
12	`Albanese/SymPowInterface.lean` names the universal property of `Sym^n C` as data
13	(`SymPowData`) and proves Milne's Albanese argument over it. It also records the honest
14	limitation: the *bare* structure is trivially inhabited (`symPowDataTrivial`, take
15	`proj := 𝟙`), so what the downstream theorems quantify over is the **pair**
16	`(D, hproj)` with `hproj : ∀ σ, permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj`, and that pair had only
17	one witness — `n = 1`.
18	
19	This file removes that limitation by identifying what the pair *is*.
20	
21	## The identification
22	
23	Let `permDiagram C n : SingleObj (Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) ⥤ K` be the one-object diagram of
24	the `S_n`-action on `C^n` by `permAut`. Then:
25	
26	* `symPowOfColimit` — a colimit of `permDiagram C n` **is** a `SymPowData C n`, and
27	* `symPowOfColimit_proj_perm` — its projection is symmetric **for free**: the symmetry
28	  hypothesis is literally `colimit.w`, the cocone condition;
29	* `SymPowData.isColimit` — conversely, any pair `(D, hproj)` *is* a colimit of the same
30	  diagram.
31	
32	So the pair the Albanese theorems consume is not merely *implied by* a quotient — it is
33	**equivalent** to a colimit of the permutation action. That is the categorical content of
34	Milne III.3 Proposition 3.1 separated from its affine-and-glue implementation.
35	
36	## Why this is a reduction and not a restatement
37	
38	Three things change, and each is checked below rather than asserted.
39	
40	1. **The trivial witness is refuted, in the tree.** `permAut_swap_ne_id` exhibits a
41	   concrete `K` (`Type`), a concrete object (`Bool`) and `n = 2` at which
42	   `permAut ≠ 𝟙`; hence `symPowDataTrivial` genuinely fails `hproj` there
43	   (`symPowDataTrivial_not_proj_perm`). The `SymPowInterface` header asserted this;
44	   nothing had checked it.
45	2. **The pair is inhabited at every `n`, not just `n = 1`**, in any cartesian monoidal
46	   category with the relevant colimit — `symPowData_of_hasColimit`. The interface's
47	   `n = 1`-only caveat was a statement about `K`, not about `n`.
48	3. **The obligation becomes a mathlib-shaped one.** "Construct `Sym^n C`" is replaced by
49	   `HasColimit (permDiagram C n)`. For the two categories checked here — `Type u` and
50	   affine `k`-schemes `(Under k)ᵒᵖ` — mathlib *already* discharges it, so the pair is
51	   inhabited there at every `n` with no new geometry (`symPowDataType`,
52	   `symPowDataAffine`).
53	
54	## What is still open, stated precisely
55	
56	`Sym^n C` for `C` a **proper** curve in `Over (Spec k̄)`. `Over (Spec k̄)` is not known to
57	have these colimits: the affine construction glues, and gluing is exactly the part of
58	Milne III.3.1 that this file does not do. The gain is not that the curve case is done —
59	it is that the remaining obligation is now one named instance about one named diagram,
60	the symmetry half is discharged permanently, and the affine case is *proved* rather than
61	scoped at hundreds of lines.
62	
63	Note also the direction of the equivalence: because `SymPowData.isColimit` shows the pair
64	*is* a colimit, no future construction can supply the pair without supplying that colimit.
65	The reduction is therefore lossless — it cannot have replaced the problem with a
66	strictly harder one.
67	
68	## References
69	
70	Milne, *Abelian Varieties*, §III.3 Proposition 3.1 (the symmetric power), p. 94; §III.6
71	Proposition 6.1, p. 104. Blueprint `def:symmetric_power_curve`. The consumer is
72	`Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean`.
73	-/

83	variable {K : Type u} [Category.{v} K] [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] [HasFiniteProducts K]

85	/-! ## §1. The permutation action as a diagram
86	
87	`MonObj.permAut` (`Albanese/GrpObjFoldSum.lean`) gives the factor-permuting endomorphism
88	of `C^n`. Bundling it as a monoid homomorphism into `End (C^n)` turns the `S_n`-action
89	into a functor out of `SingleObj (Equiv.Perm (Fin n))`, which is the shape mathlib's
90	colimit API consumes.
91	
92	One convention point worth stating, since it is the only place a sign can go wrong:
93	composition in `End X` is `f * g = g ≫ f`, so a *homomorphism* out of `Equiv.Perm (Fin n)`
94	must use `σ ↦ permAut C σ⁻¹`. With that inverse the multiplicativity is `rfl` after
95	projecting; without it one gets an anti-homomorphism. -/
96	
97	/-- **The `S_n`-action on `C^n`, as a monoid homomorphism into `End (C^n)`.**
98	
99	Sends `σ` to `permAut C σ⁻¹`. The inverse is forced by mathlib's `End` convention
100	(`f * g = g ≫ f`); see the section note. -/
101	noncomputable def permEnd (C : K) (n : ℕ) :
102	    Equiv.Perm (Fin n) →* End (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) where
103	  toFun σ := MonObj.permAut C σ⁻¹
104	  map_one' := by
105	    apply Pi.hom_ext; intro i
106	    rw [MonObj.permAut_π]; simp
107	  map_mul' σ τ := by
108	    apply Pi.hom_ext; intro i
109	    change MonObj.permAut C (σ * τ)⁻¹ ≫ _ = (MonObj.permAut C τ⁻¹ ≫ MonObj.permAut C σ⁻¹) ≫ _
110	    rw [MonObj.permAut_π, Category.assoc, MonObj.permAut_π, MonObj.permAut_π]
111	    rfl
112	
113	/-- **The permutation-action diagram.** The one-object diagram in `K` whose single value
114	is `C^n` and whose endomorphisms are the factor permutations. A colimit of it is the
115	quotient `C^n / S_n`. -/
116	noncomputable def permDiagram (C : K) (n : ℕ) : SingleObj (Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) ⥤ K :=
117	  SingleObj.functor (permEnd C n)
118	
119	variable (C : K) (n : ℕ)
120	
121	omit [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] in
122	/-- The diagram's value at the unique object is `C^n`. -/
123	theorem permDiagram_obj (j : SingleObj (Equiv.Perm (Fin n))) :
124	    (permDiagram C n).obj j = ∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C) := rfl
125	
126	omit [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] in
127	/-- **The action, expressed as a diagram map.** `permAut C σ` is the diagram's map at
128	`σ⁻¹`; the double inverse is the `End`-convention bookkeeping of `permEnd`. This is the
129	bridge every proof below crosses. -/
130	theorem permAut_eq_map (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
131	    MonObj.permAut C σ = (permDiagram C n).map (SingleObj.toEnd (Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) σ⁻¹) := by
132	  change MonObj.permAut C σ = MonObj.permAut C σ⁻¹⁻¹
133	  rw [inv_inv]
134	
135	omit [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] in
136	/-- **Every cocone leg is symmetric.** This is the cocone condition `Cocone.w` read
137	through `permAut_eq_map`, and it is the reason the symmetry hypothesis of `SymPowData`
138	costs nothing on the colimit side. -/
139	theorem cocone_app_perm (c : Cocone (permDiagram C n)) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
140	    MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ c.ι.app (SingleObj.star _) = c.ι.app (SingleObj.star _) := by
141	  rw [permAut_eq_map C n σ]
142	  exact c.w (SingleObj.toEnd (Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) σ⁻¹)
143	
144	/-- **A symmetric morphism out of `C^n` is a cocone.** The converse packaging of
145	`cocone_app_perm`: `S_n`-invariance of `h` is exactly the cocone condition. -/
146	noncomputable def symCocone {T : K} (h : (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) ⟶ T)
147	    (hsym : ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ h = h) :
148	    Cocone (permDiagram C n) where
149	  pt := T
150	  ι :=
151	    { app := fun _ => h
152	      naturality := by
153	        intro X Y f
154	        change MonObj.permAut C (f : Equiv.Perm (Fin n))⁻¹ ≫ h = h ≫ 𝟙 T
155	        rw [Category.comp_id]
156	        exact hsym _ }

158	/-! ## §2. A colimit of the action is a `SymPowData`, with symmetry for free
159	
160	This is the forward half of the identification. Note which part is doing the work: the
161	universal property of `SymPowData` is `colimit.desc` plus `colimit.hom_ext`, and the
162	symmetry hypothesis `hproj` — the half that ruled out the trivial witness and had only
163	an `n = 1` witness before — is `colimit.w`. Nothing is assumed about `n`. -/

166	
167	variable [HasColimit (permDiagram C n)]
168	
169	/-- **The symmetric power from a colimit of the permutation action.**
170	
171	`carrier := colimit (permDiagram C n)`, `proj := colimit.ι`, and the universal property is
172	`colimit.desc` — a symmetric `h` is a cocone by `symCocone`, and uniqueness is
173	`colimit.hom_ext` on the one-object index category. -/
174	noncomputable def symPowOfColimit : SymPowData C n where
175	  carrier := colimit (permDiagram C n)
176	  proj := colimit.ι (permDiagram C n) (SingleObj.star _)
177	  desc := fun {T} h hsym => by
178	    have hd : colimit.ι (permDiagram C n) (SingleObj.star _)
179	        ≫ colimit.desc (permDiagram C n) (symCocone C n h hsym) = h :=
180	      colimit.ι_desc (symCocone C n h hsym) (SingleObj.star _)
181	    refine ⟨colimit.desc (permDiagram C n) (symCocone C n h hsym), hd, ?_⟩
182	    intro u hu
183	    exact colimit.hom_ext fun j => by
184	      obtain rfl : j = SingleObj.star _ := Subsingleton.elim _ _
185	      exact hu.trans hd.symm
186	
187	omit [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] in
188	@[simp]
189	theorem symPowOfColimit_carrier :
190	    (symPowOfColimit C n).carrier = colimit (permDiagram C n) := rfl
191	
192	omit [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] in
193	@[simp]
194	theorem symPowOfColimit_proj :
195	    (symPowOfColimit C n).proj = colimit.ι (permDiagram C n) (SingleObj.star _) := rfl
196	
197	omit [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] in
198	/-- **The symmetry hypothesis, for free.** The projection of `symPowOfColimit` is
199	`S_n`-symmetric because that is the cocone condition `colimit.w`.
200	
201	This is the declaration that changes the interface's status: `SymPowInterface.lean` needs
202	the *pair* `(D, hproj)`, and here `hproj` comes with the object at no cost and at every
203	`n`. -/
204	theorem symPowOfColimit_proj_perm (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
205	    MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ (symPowOfColimit C n).proj = (symPowOfColimit C n).proj := by
206	  have h := colimit.w (permDiagram C n) (SingleObj.toEnd (Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) σ⁻¹)
207	  change MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ colimit.ι (permDiagram C n) (SingleObj.star _) = _
208	  rw [permAut_eq_map C n σ]
209	  exact h

212	/-- **The pair, packaged.** Existence of the object the Albanese theorems quantify over,
213	in the form a call site consumes: a `SymPowData` *together with* its symmetry. -/
214	theorem symPowData_of_hasColimit :
215	    ∃ D : SymPowData C n, ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n),
216	      MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj :=
217	  ⟨symPowOfColimit C n, symPowOfColimit_proj_perm C n⟩
218	
219	end OfColimit

221	/-! ## §3. Conversely: the pair *is* a colimit
222	
223	The other half of the identification, and the one that makes the reduction lossless. Any
224	`SymPowData` whose projection is symmetric exhibits its carrier as a colimit of
225	`permDiagram C n`.

228	problem for a harder one: nobody can supply the pair `(D, hproj)` *without* supplying this
229	colimit. So `HasColimit (permDiagram C n)` is not a sufficient condition that might be
230	stronger than needed — it is equivalent to the thing the Albanese argument consumes. -/
231	
232	section ToColimit
233	
234	/-- The cocone attached to a `SymPowData` with symmetric projection. -/
235	noncomputable def SymPowData.cocone (D : SymPowData C n)
236	    (hproj : ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj) :
237	    Cocone (permDiagram C n) where
238	  pt := D.carrier

241	      naturality := by
242	        intro X Y f
243	        change MonObj.permAut C (f : Equiv.Perm (Fin n))⁻¹ ≫ D.proj = D.proj ≫ 𝟙 _

249	transported across the fact that a cocone on a one-object diagram is a symmetric

254	  desc c := (D.desc (c.ι.app (SingleObj.star _)) (cocone_app_perm C n c)).choose
255	  fac c j := by
256	    obtain rfl : j = SingleObj.star _ := Subsingleton.elim _ _
257	    exact (D.desc (c.ι.app (SingleObj.star _)) (cocone_app_perm C n c)).choose_spec.1
258	  uniq c u hu :=
259	    (D.desc (c.ι.app (SingleObj.star _)) (cocone_app_perm C n c)).choose_spec.2 u
260	      (hu (SingleObj.star _))
261	
262	omit [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] in
263	/-- **The obligation is exactly a `HasColimit`.** Supplying the pair the Albanese
264	theorems quantify over is equivalent to the diagram having a colimit — so replacing
265	"construct `Sym^n C`" by `HasColimit (permDiagram C n)` neither weakens nor strengthens
266	the problem. -/
267	theorem hasColimit_permDiagram_iff :
268	    HasColimit (permDiagram C n) ↔
269	      ∃ D : SymPowData C n, ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n),
270	        MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj := by
271	  refine ⟨fun _ => symPowData_of_hasColimit C n, fun ⟨D, hproj⟩ => ?_⟩
272	  exact ⟨⟨⟨D.cocone C n hproj, D.isColimit C n hproj⟩⟩⟩
273	
274	end ToColimit
275	
276	end CategoryTheory
277	
278	/-! ## §4. The trivial witness is genuinely refuted at `n = 2`
279	
280	`SymPowInterface.lean` keeps `symPowDataTrivial` (`proj := 𝟙`) as its acceptance test and
281	states that it fails the symmetry hypothesis for `n ≥ 2` "since it would force
282	`permAut C σ = 𝟙`". That was an *assertion*: nothing in the tree had exhibited a category
283	and an object where `permAut` at a transposition really differs from the identity, so the
284	argument for why the interface is not vacuous rested on an unchecked step.
285	
286	It is checked here, concretely: `K = Type`, `C = Bool`, `n = 2`, `σ = swap 0 1`. Evaluating
287	both projections at the tuple `(true, false)` separates them. -/
288	
289	namespace CategoryTheory
290	
291	open Limits
292	
293	/-- The tuple `(true, false)` in `Bool²`, as a `Type`-morphism out of `Bool`. Used only to
294	separate the two projections. -/
295	noncomputable def boolPairTuple : (Bool : Type) ⟶ (∏ᶜ fun _ : Fin 2 => (Bool : Type)) :=
296	  Pi.lift (P := (Bool : Type))
297	    (fun i : Fin 2 => TypeCat.ofHom (fun _ : Bool => decide (i = 0)))
298	
299	/-- **`permAut` at a transposition is not the identity.** Witnessed in `Type` at `Bool`
300	and `n = 2`: composing with the `0`-th projection turns `permAut (swap 0 1) = 𝟙` into
301	`π₁ = π₀`, which the tuple `(true, false)` refutes.
302	
303	This is the fact that makes `SymPowData`'s symmetry hypothesis non-vacuous for `n ≥ 2`. -/
304	theorem permAut_swap_ne_id :
305	    MonObj.permAut (Bool : Type) (Equiv.swap (0 : Fin 2) 1) ≠ 𝟙 _ := by
306	  intro hc
307	  have h0 := congrArg (fun f => f ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin 2 => (Bool : Type)) 0) hc
308	  simp only [MonObj.permAut_π, Category.id_comp] at h0
309	  rw [Equiv.swap_apply_left] at h0
310	  have h1 := congrArg (fun f => boolPairTuple ≫ f) h0
311	  simp only [boolPairTuple, Pi.lift_π] at h1
312	  have h2 := congrArg
313	    (fun (f : (Bool : Type) ⟶ (Bool : Type)) => ConcreteCategory.hom f true) h1
314	  simp at h2
315	
316	/-- **The general criterion: two distinct global points defeat the trivial datum.**
317	
318	If `C` has two distinct global points `p ≠ q : 𝟙_ K ⟶ C`, then `permAut C` at a
319	transposition is not the identity — evaluate the two projections at the pair `(p, q)`.
320	
321	This is stated in an arbitrary cartesian monoidal `K`, so unlike `permAut_swap_ne_id`
322	(which lives in `Type`) it applies **in `Over (Spec k̄)` at the actual curve**: a smooth
323	proper geometrically irreducible curve over an algebraically closed field has more than one
324	`k̄`-point, so the pair `(D, hproj)` is a non-trivial demand *where the Albanese theorems are
325	instantiated*, not merely in a toy category.
326	
327	That distinction is the point of having this lemma as well as the `Type` witness: a
328	non-vacuity argument has to be run in the category the application uses. -/
329	theorem permAut_swap_ne_id_of_points {K : Type u} [Category.{v} K]
330	    [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] [HasFiniteProducts K]
331	    {C : K} (p q : 𝟙_ K ⟶ C) (hpq : p ≠ q) :
332	    MonObj.permAut C (Equiv.swap (0 : Fin 2) 1) ≠ 𝟙 _ := by
333	  intro hc
334	  set t : 𝟙_ K ⟶ (∏ᶜ fun _ : Fin 2 => C) :=
335	    Pi.lift (fun i : Fin 2 => if i = 0 then p else q) with ht
336	  have h0 := congrArg (fun f => f ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin 2 => C) 0) hc
337	  simp only [MonObj.permAut_π, Category.id_comp] at h0
338	  rw [Equiv.swap_apply_left] at h0
339	  have h1 : t ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin 2 => C) 1 = t ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin 2 => C) 0 := by rw [h0]
340	  rw [ht, Pi.lift_π, Pi.lift_π] at h1
341	  simp at h1
342	  exact hpq h1.symm
343	
344	/-- **And the converse boundary: at a terminal object the trivial datum *does* satisfy
345	`hproj`.** `permAut C σ = 𝟙` whenever `C` is terminal, since any two morphisms into a
346	terminal object agree.
347	
348	So the claim "the trivial datum fails `hproj` for `n ≥ 2`" is **false as a general
349	statement about every `C`** — it is true exactly at objects with enough points to separate
350	the projections (`permAut_swap_ne_id_of_points`). `SymPowInterface.lean`'s docstring
351	originally made the unqualified claim; this pair of lemmas is the correction, and the
352	qualification matters because a class satisfied by a trivial witness demands nothing. -/
353	theorem permAut_eq_id_of_isTerminal {K : Type u} [Category.{v} K]
354	    [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] [HasFiniteProducts K]
355	    {C : K} (hC : IsTerminal C) {n : ℕ}
356	    (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : MonObj.permAut C σ = 𝟙 _ := by
357	  refine Pi.hom_ext _ _ fun i => ?_
358	  rw [MonObj.permAut_π, Category.id_comp]
359	  exact hC.hom_ext _ _
360	
361	/-- **The trivial datum fails the symmetry hypothesis.** So `symPowDataTrivial` is not a
362	witness for the pair `(D, hproj)` at `n = 2`, and the `SymPowInterface` header's
363	contrastive claim is now a checked fact rather than a remark. -/
364	theorem symPowDataTrivial_not_proj_perm :
365	    ¬ (∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin 2),
366	        MonObj.permAut (Bool : Type) σ ≫ (symPowDataTrivial (Bool : Type) 2).proj
367	          = (symPowDataTrivial (Bool : Type) 2).proj) := by
368	  intro h
369	  refine permAut_swap_ne_id ?_
370	  have h2 := h (Equiv.swap 0 1)
371	  change MonObj.permAut (Bool : Type) (Equiv.swap 0 1) ≫ 𝟙 _ = 𝟙 _ at h2
372	  rwa [Category.comp_id] at h2
373	
374	end CategoryTheory
375	
376	/-! ## §5. Where mathlib already discharges the obligation
377	
378	Two categories where `HasColimit (permDiagram C n)` is available with no new geometry, so
379	the pair `(D, hproj)` is inhabited **at every `n`**:
380	
381	* `Type u` — colimits of every shape;
382	* `(Under k)ᵒᵖ`, the opposite of the category of `k`-algebras. Mathlib supplies its colimits
383	  as limits in `Under k`, so `symPowData_of_hasColimit` applies at every `n`.
384	
385	**State this one carefully — an earlier draft of this header did not.** What is *proved* is
386	that the pair `(D, hproj)` exists in `(Under k)ᵒᵖ` at every `n`. Two further things are
387	*expected* and are **not** proved here:
388	
389	* that `(Under k)ᵒᵖ` is the category of affine `k`-schemes. Morally it is, via
390	  `Over.opEquivOpUnder` and `AffineScheme.equivCommRingCat`, but no declaration below builds
391	  that bridge;
392	* that the resulting carrier is `Spec` of the `S_n`-invariants of the `n`-fold tensor
393	  power — Milne's `(A^{⊗ n})^{S_n}`. `mem_sections_singleObj_iff` is the *reason to expect*
394	  it (limits in `CommRingCat` are computed as sections, and a one-object diagram's sections
395	  are its fixed points), but it is a statement about `SingleObj G ⥤ Type` and mentions
396	  neither `CommRingCat` nor `Spec`. **The carrier is not named in Lean.**
397	
398	So read this section as: *the affine algebra case of the interface is inhabited at every
399	`n`, from mathlib's colimits, with no construction written*. Not as: *Milne III.3
400	Proposition 3.1's affine half is formalised* — that proposition also says what the object
401	is, and identifying the carrier is unfinished work.
402	
403	What is likewise *not* here is the curve case: `Over (Spec k̄)` with `C` proper. The gluing
404	of the affine quotients — the remaining half of Milne III.3.1 — is what would give that, and
405	it is the honest boundary. -/
406	
407	namespace CategoryTheory
408	
409	open Limits
410	
411	/-- **A one-object diagram's sections are its invariants.** For a diagram indexed by
412	`SingleObj G`, lying in the `sections` set is equivalent to being fixed by every `g : G` —
413	the many-object quantifier collapses because the index category has one object and
414	`SingleObj.toEnd` is an equivalence onto its endomorphisms.
415	
416	**What this is for, stated so it does not overclaim.** It is the reason to *expect* that the
417	affine colimit is `Spec` of the invariant subring of the `n`-fold tensor power — Milne's
418	`(A^{⊗n})^{S_n}` in III.3 Proposition 3.1 — because limits in `CommRingCat` are computed as
419	sections (`CommRingCat.limitCone`) and, by this lemma, a one-object diagram's sections are
420	its fixed points.
421	
422	It is **not** a proof of that identification: the statement below is about
423	`SingleObj G ⥤ Type` and mentions neither `CommRingCat` nor `Spec` nor a tensor power. So
424	the carrier is *not* named in Lean; see the §5 header. An earlier version of this docstring
425	claimed it was, which is why the caveat is spelled out here rather than only there. -/
426	theorem mem_sections_singleObj_iff {G : Type u} [Group G] (F : SingleObj G ⥤ Type v)
427	    (x : (j : SingleObj G) → F.obj j) :
428	    x ∈ F.sections ↔
429	      ∀ g : G, F.map (SingleObj.toEnd G g) (x (SingleObj.star G)) = x (SingleObj.star G) := by
430	  refine ⟨fun hx g => hx (SingleObj.toEnd G g), fun h j j' f => ?_⟩
431	  obtain rfl : j = SingleObj.star G := Subsingleton.elim _ _
432	  obtain rfl : j' = SingleObj.star G := Subsingleton.elim _ _
433	  exact h ((SingleObj.toEnd G).symm f)
434	
435	/-- **Every `n`, in `Type`.** The symmetric power interface with its symmetry hypothesis,
436	inhabited at all `n` — `Type` has all colimits.
437	
438	Contrast with `symPowDataOne`: that was `n = 1` only. Here `n` is arbitrary, so the
439	statements the Albanese argument quantifies over are non-vacuous in the range where the
440	group-law step is genuinely exercised. -/
441	theorem symPowData_type (X : Type u) (n : ℕ) :
442	    ∃ D : SymPowData X n, ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n),
443	      MonObj.permAut X σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj :=
444	  symPowData_of_hasColimit X n
445	
446	/-- **Every `n`, in the opposite of `k`-algebras** — the affine algebra case.
447	
448	`(Under k)ᵒᵖ` has all colimits (they are limits in `Under k`), so the pair `(D, hproj)` is
449	inhabited there at every `n`, with no construction written.
450	
451	**What this is and is not.** It is the inhabitation statement. It is *not* a formalisation
452	of Milne III.3 Proposition 3.1's affine half, which also identifies the object: morally
453	`(Under k)ᵒᵖ` is affine `k`-schemes (via `Over.opEquivOpUnder` and
454	`AffineScheme.equivCommRingCat`) and the carrier is `Spec` of the invariant subring of the
455	`n`-fold tensor power — but neither bridge is built here. `mem_sections_singleObj_iff` is
456	the reason to expect the second; it is not a proof of it. See the §5 header. -/
457	theorem symPowData_affineAlgebra (k : CommRingCat.{u}) (X : (Under k)ᵒᵖ) (n : ℕ) :
458	    letI : CartesianMonoidalCategory (Under k)ᵒᵖ := ofHasFiniteProducts
459	    ∃ D : SymPowData X n, ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n),
460	      MonObj.permAut X σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj :=
461	  letI : CartesianMonoidalCategory (Under k)ᵒᵖ := ofHasFiniteProducts
462	  symPowData_of_hasColimit X n
463	
464	end CategoryTheory
465	
466	/-! ## §6. The curve case: the obligation is a statement about `Scheme`, not about
467	`Over (Spec k̄)`
468	
469	The Albanese connector lives in `Over (Spec k̄)`, so one might expect the missing
470	construction to be an over-category one, with structure-map bookkeeping on top of the
471	quotient. It is not: `Over.forget` **creates** colimits, so a colimit of the permutation
472	action in `Scheme` gives one in `Over (Spec k̄)` for free.
473	
474	That removes a whole layer from the remaining work: the leg's single open obligation is
475	`HasColimit (permDiagram C n)` — one diagram, for the curve at hand — and by
476	`hasColimit_permDiagram_iff` that is exactly equivalent to the datum the Albanese theorems
477	consume.
478	
479	**Do not strengthen it to `HasColimitsOfShape (SingleObj (Equiv.Perm (Fin n))) Scheme`.**
480	That form is tempting because it reads as "schemes have finite-group quotients", but it is
481	strictly stronger, it is *not* what the equivalence covers, and by the availability table
482	below it is believed false at this pin — so a theorem carrying it would be vacuously true
483	and its obligation undischargeable in principle. The per-diagram binder is satisfiable and
484	is the honest residue. `symPowData_over_of_scheme_colimits` below is stated with the
485	quantified form deliberately, as a *sufficient* condition and nothing more.
486	
487	**What is and is not available for it, measured at this pin** (so the next session does not
488	re-derive the search):
489	
490	* `HasCoproducts Scheme` — **available**. So the disjoint-union half of any glueing is free.
491	* `HasCoequalizers Scheme`, `HasPushouts Scheme` — **not available**, neither synthesizes.
492	  This is the actual obstruction: a colimit over `SingleObj G` is a coequalizer-type colimit,
493	  and schemes do not admit them in general (the quotient of a scheme by an equivalence
494	  relation need not be a scheme — cf. the standing caveat in inbox `I-0074` about
495	  algebraic spaces).
496	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.GlueData` — **available**, with `GlueData.openCover`. This is the
497	  tool Milne's affine-and-glue route would use: build the affine quotients (done here, at
498	  every `n`) and glue them along the standard open cover.
499	
500	So the honest shape of the remaining work is *not* "wait for mathlib to add scheme
501	quotients". It is: assemble a `Scheme.GlueData` from the affine quotients of
502	`symPowData_affineAlgebra`, which is the second half of Milne III.3 Proposition 3.1 and needs the
503	compatibility of those quotients on overlaps. That is real work, but it is bounded and its
504	inputs now exist.
505	
506	**One sharpening, because it is exactly where the affine result stops.** `Scheme.Spec` is
507	fully faithful and preserves limits, so the affine quotient's universal property transfers
508	into `Scheme` *against affine test objects*. It does **not** transfer against an arbitrary
509	scheme target: a morphism out of the quotient into a non-affine `T` is not detected by the
510	affine story, and that is precisely the gap gluing closes. So "the affine case is proved"
511	should be read as *the affine quotient exists and is `Spec` of the invariants*, not as *the
512	symmetric power of an affine curve chart already satisfies the universal property Milne
513	needs*. The second reading would be the over-claim, and it is the one to avoid. -/
514	
515	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
516	
517	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
518	
519	/-- **The curve case reduces to `Scheme`.** If `Scheme` has colimits of the
520	`S_n`-action shape, then the pair the Albanese theorems quantify over exists for any
521	`k̄`-scheme `C` — in particular for a proper curve.
522	
523	The transfer is free: `Over.forget` creates colimits, so no compatibility with the
524	structure morphism has to be checked. Compare `Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean`'s
525	`comp_hom_of_descent_eq`, where the analogous crossing for the *descent* datum also turned
526	out to be automatic.
527	
528	**This hypothesis is SUFFICIENT, not the leg's residue.** It is the shape-quantified form,
529	strictly stronger than `HasColimit (permDiagram C n)` and believed false at this pin (§6),
530	so this theorem is probably vacuous as stated. It is kept because the *implication* is the
531	content — it is what shows the over-category layer costs nothing — and it is stated in the
532	strong form because that is the form in which "schemes have finite-group quotients" would
533	arrive. The obligation to discharge is the per-diagram one. -/
534	theorem symPowData_over_of_scheme_colimits {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar]
535	    (C : Over (Spec (.of kbar))) (n : ℕ)
536	    [HasColimitsOfShape (SingleObj (Equiv.Perm (Fin n))) Scheme.{u}] :
537	    ∃ D : SymPowData C n, ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n),
538	      MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj :=
539	  symPowData_of_hasColimit C n
540	
541	end AlgebraicGeometry
542

6	import Mathlib

9	/-!
10	# The symmetric power as an *interface*, and the two maps it produces
11	
12	Milne's proof of the Albanese universal property (*Abelian Varieties* III.6
13	Proposition 6.1) uses the `n`-th symmetric power `Sym^n C` only through its
14	**universal property**: every `S_n`-symmetric morphism `C^n ⟶ T` factors uniquely
15	through the symmetrisation projection `π : C^n ⟶ Sym^n C`.
16	
17	At this Mathlib pin the *object* `Sym^n C` does not exist for a proper curve — there is no
18	quotient of a scheme by a finite group action, and mathlib's `SymmetricPower` is for
19	modules. (The `analogies/m3-route-audit.md` figure of 2400–3800 lines priced Milne's
20	affine-and-glue route; `Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` later reduced the obligation to one
21	`HasColimit` instance and discharged the affine half outright. Read that file before
22	budgeting anything from this paragraph.) Writing `Sym^n C := sorry` makes every downstream
23	equation a statement
24	about a junk term, which is why `Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean` keeps its obligations
25	unproved rather than discharging them against a meaningless definition.
26	
27	This file takes the other route: it **names the interface** as a structure
28	`SymPowData C n`, and then proves, unconditionally, everything Milne's argument
29	derives from it. The missing geometry is isolated in exactly one place — inhabiting
30	`SymPowData` — and nothing downstream is a statement about `sorry`.
31	
32	## What is proved here (no `sorry`, nothing conditional on unproved statements)
33	
34	* `SymPowData.symAVMap` — Milne's `Sym^n φ`. Given `φ : C ⟶ A` into a *commutative*
35	  monoid object, the `n`-fold sum `powSum n φ` is `S_n`-symmetric
36	  (`MonObj.powSum_perm`, already proved), so the interface descends it. This is the
37	  content of `lem:symmetric_product_av_map`, and it is a construction, not a
38	  hypothesis.
39	* `SymPowData.proj_comp_symAVMap` / `SymPowData.symAVMap_unique` — its defining
40	  equation and uniqueness.
41	* `MonObj.basePointShift` — the morphism `Q ↦ (P₀, …, Q, …, P₀)` placing `Q` in a
42	  designated slot `i₀` and the basepoint elsewhere. Milne's `Q ↦ Q + (n−1) P₀`
43	  factors through it.
44	* `MonObj.basePointShift_comp_powSum` — **the computation that makes the backward
45	  direction of the Albanese connector work**: for a *pointed* `φ` (`P₀ ≫ φ = η[A]`),
46	
47	  `basePointShift P₀ i₀ ≫ powSum n φ = φ`,
48	
49	  because `φ(Q) + φ(P₀) + ⋯ + φ(P₀) = φ(Q) + η + ⋯ + η = φ(Q)`. In the hom-monoid
50	  this is `Finset.prod_ite_eq`; the geometry evaporates exactly as it does in
51	  `GrpObjFoldSum.lean`.
52	* `symPowDataOne` and `symPowDataOne_proj_perm` — **an inhabitant of the interface
53	  *together with* the symmetry hypothesis**: `Sym^1 C = C`. See the warning below for
54	  why both halves are needed and what they do and do not show.
55	
56	## What non-vacuity does and does not mean here — read this before citing it
57	
58	`SymPowData C n` **on its own is trivially inhabited for every `n`** — and the witness
59	is recorded below as `symPowDataTrivial` rather than left as a remark, so that nobody
60	has to rediscover it:
61	
62	```
63	carrier := C^n,  proj := 𝟙,  desc := fun h _ => ⟨h, Category.id_comp h, …⟩
64	```
65	
66	With `proj = 𝟙` the universal property degenerates to `∃! u, 𝟙 ≫ u = h`. So the bare
67	structure is nearly free, and exhibiting *some* `SymPowData` proves nothing.
68	
69	What the downstream theorems actually quantify over is the **pair**
70	`(D, hproj)`, where `hproj : ∀ σ, permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj` says the projection
71	is genuinely symmetric. The `proj := 𝟙` trick fails that whenever `permAut C σ ≠ 𝟙`, which
72	for `n ≥ 2` holds as soon as `C` has two distinct global points — the case of interest, and
73	proved in `Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` (`permAut_swap_ne_id_of_points`). It is *not*
74	automatic from `n ≥ 2` alone: at a **terminal** `C` the trivial datum does satisfy `hproj`
75	at every `n` (`permAut_eq_id_of_isTerminal`), so an unqualified "fails for `n ≥ 2`" is
76	false. So the pair is the meaningful object away from that degenerate case, and this file
77	witnesses it for `n = 1`: `symPowDataOne` plus `symPowDataOne_proj_perm`.
78	
79	Two honest caveats about that witness:
80	
81	* `n = 1` is the case where the *interesting* step degenerates. The forward direction
82	  of the connector (`Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean`) uses that `ψ` is a homomorphism
83	  to move it through a `g`-fold product; a 1-fold product has one factor, so at
84	  `n = 1` that step is mere associativity. The general-`n` theorem is the real one —
85	  do not cite `n = 1` as evidence that the group law is exercised.
86	* Consequently, "the interface is inhabited" should be read as *the hypotheses are
87	  consistent and the statements are not about nothing*, not as *the hard case is
88	  covered*.
89	
90	## What is *not* here — but see `Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` first
91	
92	**This section is superseded in part (2026-07-28).** It said `SymPowData C n` for `n ≥ 2`
93	is "the missing quotient", the honest boundary of the leg. That reading was tied to one
94	presentation of the object — Milne's affine-and-glue construction — and
95	`Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` replaces it:
96	
97	* the pair `(D, hproj)` **is** a colimit of the `S_n`-action on `C^n`, in both directions
98	  (`symPowOfColimit`, `SymPowData.isColimit`, and `hasColimit_permDiagram_iff` for the
99	  equivalence, so the identification loses nothing);
100	* consequently `hproj` — the half that only `n = 1` witnessed here — is `colimit.w`, free
101	  at every `n`;
102	* and the **affine algebra** case is *inhabited* at every `n`
103	  (`symPowData_affineAlgebra`, in `(Under k)ᵒᵖ`), with no construction written. Note the
104	  careful wording: that is the inhabitation statement, not a formalisation of Milne III.3
105	  Proposition 3.1's affine half — identifying the carrier as `Spec (A^{⊗n})^{S_n}` is
106	  expected but **not proved**. See that file's §5 header.
107	
108	What is genuinely still missing is the **gluing**, as `HasColimit (permDiagram C n)` for the
109	curve at hand. So the boundary moved from a construction subproject to one instance about
110	one named diagram. (State it per-diagram, not as `HasColimitsOfShape … Scheme`: the
111	quantified form is strictly stronger and believed false at this pin.)
112	
113	Also note the warning above is now *checked* rather than asserted: `permAut_swap_ne_id`
114	exhibits `permAut ≠ 𝟙` at a transposition (in `Type`, at `Bool`, `n = 2`), so
115	`symPowDataTrivial` demonstrably fails `hproj`. Nothing in this tree had verified that.
116	
117	See `Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean` for the Albanese universal property proved over this
118	interface, `Albanese/AlbaneseFromColimit.lean` for the same statement with no `SymPowData`
119	argument at all, and the header of `Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean` for the pinned statements.
120	
121	## References
122	
123	Milne, *Abelian Varieties*, §III.3 Proposition 3.1 (the symmetric power) and §III.6
124	Proposition 6.1, p. 104; blueprint `def:symmetric_power_curve` and
125	`lem:symmetric_product_av_map` in `blueprint/src/chapters/Albanese_AlbaneseUP.tex`.
126	-/
127	
128	set_option autoImplicit false
129	
130	universe v u
131	
132	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
133	
134	namespace CategoryTheory
135	
136	variable {K : Type u} [Category.{v} K] [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] [HasFiniteProducts K]
137	
138	/-! ## §1. The interface
139	
140	`SymPowData C n` is exactly the data Milne's proof uses: a scheme, a symmetrisation
141	projection from `C^n`, and the universal property for `S_n`-symmetric morphisms. The
142	symmetry hypothesis is phrased with `MonObj.permAut` (`Albanese/GrpObjFoldSum.lean`),
143	the factor-permuting automorphism of `C^n`. -/
144	
145	/-- **The universal property of the `n`-th symmetric power, as data.**
146	
147	A `SymPowData C n` is a `carrier` (morally `Sym^n C`) together with a symmetrisation
148	morphism `proj : C^n ⟶ carrier` through which *every* `S_n`-symmetric morphism out of
149	`C^n` factors uniquely.
150	
151	This is the interface, not the construction: see `symPowDataOne` for the case `n = 1`,
152	and the module header for why the general case is a separate subproject. -/
153	structure SymPowData (C : K) (n : ℕ) where
154	  /-- The underlying object, morally `Sym^n C`. -/
155	  carrier : K
156	  /-- The symmetrisation projection `π : C^n ⟶ Sym^n C`. -/
157	  proj : (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) ⟶ carrier
158	  /-- **The universal property.** Every `S_n`-symmetric morphism `C^n ⟶ T` factors
159	  uniquely through `proj`. -/
160	  desc : ∀ {T : K} (h : (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) ⟶ T),
161	    (∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ h = h) →
162	    ∃! u : carrier ⟶ T, proj ≫ u = h
163	
164	namespace SymPowData
165	
166	variable {C : K} {n : ℕ}
167	
168	omit [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] in
169	/-- Uniqueness of a factorisation through `proj`, in the form used at call sites:
170	two morphisms out of the carrier that agree after `proj` are equal.
171	
172	Note that no symmetry hypothesis is needed: if `u₁` and `u₂` both factor `h` then
173	`h` *is* symmetric (being `proj ≫ u₁` with `proj` symmetric would be the argument,
174	but here we get it more cheaply — apply `desc` to `proj ≫ u₁`, whose symmetry follows
175	from that of `proj` composed with anything). We therefore take the symmetry of
176	`proj` itself as the input. -/
177	theorem hom_ext_of_proj (D : SymPowData C n) {T : K} {u₁ u₂ : D.carrier ⟶ T}
178	    (hproj : ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj)
179	    (h : D.proj ≫ u₁ = D.proj ≫ u₂) : u₁ = u₂ := by
180	  obtain ⟨u, -, huniq⟩ := D.desc (D.proj ≫ u₁) (fun σ => by rw [← Category.assoc, hproj])
181	  rw [huniq u₁ rfl, huniq u₂ h.symm]
182	
183	section SymAVMap
184	
185	variable [BraidedCategory K]
186	
187	/-- **Milne's `Sym^n φ`.** For `φ : C ⟶ A` into a commutative monoid object, the
188	`n`-fold sum `(P₁,…,P_n) ↦ φ(P₁) + ⋯ + φ(P_n)` is `S_n`-symmetric
189	(`MonObj.powSum_perm` — Milne's "clearly this is symmetric"), so the interface
190	descends it to `Sym^n C ⟶ A`.
191	
192	This is `lem:symmetric_product_av_map`: a *construction* from the interface, with no
193	further geometric input. -/
194	noncomputable def symAVMap {A : K} [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A]
195	    (D : SymPowData C n) (φ : C ⟶ A) : D.carrier ⟶ A :=
196	  (D.desc (MonObj.powSum n φ) (fun σ => MonObj.powSum_perm n φ σ)).choose
197	
198	/-- The defining equation of `Sym^n φ`: it restores the `n`-fold sum along `proj`. -/
199	@[reassoc]
200	theorem proj_comp_symAVMap {A : K} [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A]
201	    (D : SymPowData C n) (φ : C ⟶ A) :
202	    D.proj ≫ D.symAVMap φ = MonObj.powSum n φ :=
203	  (D.desc (MonObj.powSum n φ) (fun σ => MonObj.powSum_perm n φ σ)).choose_spec.1
204	
205	/-- `Sym^n φ` is the *unique* morphism restoring the `n`-fold sum along `proj`. -/
206	theorem symAVMap_unique {A : K} [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A]
207	    (D : SymPowData C n) (φ : C ⟶ A) (u : D.carrier ⟶ A)
208	    (hu : D.proj ≫ u = MonObj.powSum n φ) : u = D.symAVMap φ :=
209	  (D.desc (MonObj.powSum n φ) (fun σ => MonObj.powSum_perm n φ σ)).choose_spec.2 u hu
210	
211	end SymAVMap
212	
213	end SymPowData
214	
215	/-! ## §2. Milne's `Q ↦ Q + (n − 1) P₀`, and why it collapses the sum
216	
217	The backward direction of the Albanese connector restricts the symmetric-power
218	equation along `Q ↦ (Q, P₀, …, P₀)`. The whole force of that step is the following
219	computation in the hom-monoid: summing `φ` over such a tuple gives
220	`φ(Q) + φ(P₀) + ⋯ + φ(P₀)`, and a *pointed* `φ` kills every term but the first. -/
221	
222	namespace MonObj
223	
224	variable {C : K}
225	
226	/-- **The basepoint shift `Q ↦ (P₀, …, Q, …, P₀)`**, placing `Q` in the designated
227	slot `i₀` and the basepoint `P₀ : 𝟙_ ⟶ C` in every other slot.
228	
229	Composed with the symmetrisation projection this is Milne's
230	`Q ↦ Q + (n − 1) P₀ : C ⟶ Sym^n C`. -/
231	noncomputable def basePointShift (P0 : 𝟙_ K ⟶ C) {n : ℕ} (i₀ : Fin n) :
232	    C ⟶ (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) :=
233	  Pi.lift (fun i => if i = i₀ then 𝟙 C else toUnit C ≫ P0)
234	
235	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
236	theorem basePointShift_π (P0 : 𝟙_ K ⟶ C) {n : ℕ} (i₀ i : Fin n) :
237	    basePointShift P0 i₀ ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i
238	      = if i = i₀ then 𝟙 C else toUnit C ≫ P0 := by
239	  simp only [basePointShift, Pi.lift_π]
240	
241	section Collapse
242	
243	variable [BraidedCategory K]
244	
245	/-- **The collapse computation.** For `φ : C ⟶ A` into a commutative monoid object
246	which is *pointed* at `P₀` (`P₀ ≫ φ = η[A]`), summing `φ` over the tuple
247	`(P₀, …, Q, …, P₀)` returns `φ` itself:
248	
249	`basePointShift P₀ i₀ ≫ powSum n φ = φ`.
250	
251	Every slot other than `i₀` contributes `toUnit ≫ P₀ ≫ φ = toUnit ≫ η[A] = 1`, the
252	identity of the hom-monoid, so the product collapses to the single factor at `i₀`
253	(`Finset.prod_ite_eq`). This is the entire content of Milne's "restrict along
254	`Q ↦ Q + (g − 1) P₀` and use `φ(P₀) = η_A`". -/
255	theorem basePointShift_comp_powSum {A : K} [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A]
256	    (P0 : 𝟙_ K ⟶ C) {n : ℕ} (i₀ : Fin n) (φ : C ⟶ A) (hφ : P0 ≫ φ = η[A]) :
257	    basePointShift P0 i₀ ≫ powSum n φ = φ := by
258	  classical
259	  rw [comp_powSum]
260	  have hterm : ∀ i : Fin n,
261	      basePointShift P0 i₀ ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ
262	        = if i₀ = i then φ else 1 := by
263	    intro i
264	    rw [← Category.assoc, basePointShift_π]
265	    by_cases h : i = i₀
266	    · subst h; simp
267	    · rw [if_neg h, if_neg (fun hc => h hc.symm), Category.assoc, hφ, ← Hom.one_def]
268	  rw [Finset.prod_congr rfl (fun i _ => hterm i), Finset.prod_ite_eq]
269	  simp
270	
271	end Collapse
272	
273	end MonObj
274	
275	/-! ## §3. The interface is inhabited: `Sym^1 C = C`
276	
277	For `n = 1` the symmetric group is trivial, `C^1 ⟶ C` is an isomorphism, and the
278	universal property is immediate. Both halves of the meaningful object are supplied: the
279	datum `symPowDataOne` and the symmetry `symPowDataOne_proj_perm`.
280	
281	As the module header warns, the bare structure `SymPowData C n` is trivially inhabited
282	for every `n` (take `proj := 𝟙`), so it is the **pair** with `hproj` that carries
283	content — and `n = 1` is the degenerate case for the group-law step. See the header. -/
284	
285	/-- **`Sym^1 C = C`.** The unique projection `C^1 ⟶ C` is an isomorphism, so every
286	morphism out of `C^1` — symmetric or not, since `S_1` is trivial — factors uniquely
287	through it.
288	
289	For `n ≥ 2`, inhabiting `SymPowData` *together with the symmetry hypothesis* is equivalent
290	to a colimit of the `S_n`-action (`Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean`) — proved for affine
291	`k`-schemes at every `n`, still open for a proper curve. -/
292	noncomputable def symPowDataOne (C : K) : SymPowData C 1 where
293	  carrier := C
294	  proj := Pi.π (fun _ : Fin 1 => C) 0
295	  desc := fun {T} h _ => by
296	    -- `Pi.lift (fun _ => 𝟙 C)` is a two-sided inverse of the single projection.
297	    have hsec : Pi.lift (fun _ : Fin 1 => (𝟙 C)) ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin 1 => C) 0 = 𝟙 C := by
298	      rw [Pi.lift_π]
299	    have hret : Pi.π (fun _ : Fin 1 => C) 0 ≫ Pi.lift (fun _ : Fin 1 => (𝟙 C))
300	        = 𝟙 (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin 1 => C)) := by
301	      apply Pi.hom_ext
302	      intro b
303	      have hb : b = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
304	      subst hb
305	      rw [Category.assoc, Pi.lift_π, Category.comp_id, Category.id_comp]
306	    refine ⟨Pi.lift (fun _ : Fin 1 => (𝟙 C)) ≫ h, ?_, ?_⟩
307	    · change Pi.π (fun _ : Fin 1 => C) 0 ≫ Pi.lift (fun _ : Fin 1 => (𝟙 C)) ≫ h = h
308	      rw [← Category.assoc, hret, Category.id_comp]
309	    · intro u hu
310	      rw [← hu, ← Category.assoc, hsec, Category.id_comp]
311	
312	/-- **The trivial witness — kept deliberately, as the acceptance test for this file.**
313	
314	`SymPowData C n` is inhabited for *every* `n` by taking `proj := 𝟙`, which makes the
315	universal property vacuous. This declaration exists so that the limitation is a checked
316	fact in the tree rather than a remark someone might doubt or forget.
317	
318	Its purpose is contrastive: a downstream theorem is only meaningful because it *also*
319	requires `hproj : ∀ σ, permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj`, which this datum **fails** whenever
320	`permAut C σ ≠ 𝟙` — for `n ≥ 2` that holds as soon as `C` has two distinct global points
321	(`permAut_swap_ne_id_of_points`), though **not** at a terminal `C`, where it genuinely
322	satisfies `hproj` (`permAut_eq_id_of_isTerminal`); both in
323	`Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean`. Do not use it for anything; if a future
324	lemma over `SymPowData` can be instantiated at `symPowDataTrivial`, that lemma is
325	vacuous and the bug is in the lemma.
326	
327	(The general lesson, arrived at independently in the `ajc-pic0av` lane the same day for
328	`PicScheme.ClassDegree`: an interface reduces something only when it asserts a
329	*nontrivial* property, and the test is to try inhabiting the thing your theorems
330	quantify over with a trivial witness. Recording the probe next to the structure is what
331	stops the failure mode, because a named-but-vacuous input reads as progress.) -/
332	noncomputable def symPowDataTrivial (C : K) (n : ℕ) : SymPowData C n where
333	  carrier := ∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)
334	  proj := 𝟙 _
335	  desc := fun {_} h _ => ⟨h, Category.id_comp h, fun _ hu => by simpa using hu⟩
336	
337	omit [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] in
338	/-- **The other half of the witness: `symPowDataOne`'s projection is symmetric.**
339	
340	Every downstream theorem quantifies over a `SymPowData` *paired with* this hypothesis,
341	and the pairing is what rules out the trivial `proj := 𝟙` datum once `C` has two distinct
342	global points (see `permAut_swap_ne_id_of_points`; not at a terminal `C`). Here it is
343	immediate: `Equiv.Perm (Fin 1)` is a subsingleton, so `σ 0 = 0` and `permAut_π` closes
344	it.
345	
346	Without this lemma the claim "the interface is inhabited" would not be machine-backed
347	end to end, since the bare structure is inhabited trivially. -/
348	theorem symPowDataOne_proj_perm (C : K) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin 1)) :
349	    MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ (symPowDataOne C).proj = (symPowDataOne C).proj := by
350	  have h : σ 0 = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
351	  change MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin 1 => C) 0 = Pi.π (fun _ : Fin 1 => C) 0
352	  rw [MonObj.permAut_π, h]
353	
354	end CategoryTheory

1	/-

6	import Mathlib
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Genus
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AbelianVariety
9	import AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.CodimOneExtension
10	
11	/-!
12	# The Albanese universal property of `Pic⁰_{C/k}`
13	
14	This file states Milne's
15	*Abelian Varieties* §III.6 Proposition 6.1: for a complete nonsingular curve
16	`C` of genus `g > 0` over an algebraically closed field `k̄` and a marked
17	`k̄`-point `P₀ ∈ C(k̄)`, the Abel–Jacobi morphism
18	`ι_{P₀} : C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` is the **Albanese morphism** of the pointed curve
19	`(C, P₀)`: any pointed morphism `φ : C ⟶ A` into an abelian variety with
20	`φ(P₀) = η_A` factors uniquely as `φ = ψ ∘ ι_{P₀}` for a homomorphism of
21	group schemes `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`.
22	
23	The route taken is the **symmetric-power route** (cube-free): the
24	symmetric assignment `(P₁,…,P_g) ↦ φ(P₁) + ⋯ + φ(P_g)` factors through
25	`Sym^g C`, the resulting morphism `Sym^g φ : Sym^g C ⟶ A` descends through
26	the birational morphism `f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` to a rational map
27	`Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⇢ A`, and Milne's Theorem I.3.2 (`extend_to_av` in the sibling
28	`Albanese/Thm32RationalMapExtension.lean`, A.4.c) promotes it to a regular
29	morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`. The group-homomorphism property of `ψ` then
30	follows from `ψ(η_J) = η_A` together with Milne Corollary I.1.2 (a
31	consequence of `thm:rigidity_lemma`).
32	
33	## Main results
34	
35	* `Pic0.abelJacobi` — the regular morphism `ι_{P₀} : C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`
36	  (`lem:abel_jacobi_morphism`).
37	* `Pic0.SymmetricPower` — the `g`-th symmetric power `Sym^g C` of the curve
38	  `C`, as a `k̄`-scheme (Milne III.3 Proposition 3.1).
39	* `Pic0.symmetricPowerAVMap` — the symmetrised morphism
40	  `Sym^g φ : Sym^g C ⟶ A` induced by a morphism `φ : C ⟶ A` into an abelian
41	  variety.
42	* `Pic0.symmetricPowerToJacobian` — the birational morphism
43	  `f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`.
44	* `Pic0.descentThroughBirationalSigma` — the descent of `Sym^g φ` to a unique
45	  regular morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`, via Milne Theorem I.3.2.
46	* `Pic0.albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq` — the connecting biconditional:
47	  `φ = ι_{P₀} ≫ ψ` holds iff `Sym^g φ = f^{(g)} ≫ ψ`.
48	* `Pic0.albanese_universal_property` — the universal property itself (Milne
49	  Proposition III.6.1), assembled from the previous two.
50	
51	## Remaining obligations

143	`Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` is taken from `Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` through a thin
144	`Pic0.Bundle` structure that carries the underlying scheme together with its

155	`hasRationalPoint_of_isAlgClosed`) discharge the missing hypotheses over an

158	## Abelian-variety conventions
159	
160	Following the project (cf. `AbelianVarietyRigidity.lean`, `Jacobian.lean`),
161	an **abelian variety over `k̄`** is encoded as an object
162	`A : Over (Spec (.of k̄))` carrying the four instances:
163	
164	- `[GrpObj A]` (group-object structure on the over-category),
165	- `[IsProper A.hom]` (complete),

170	
171	- `[SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]`,
