193	/-! ## §0.0. Substrate bridges: geometric integrality and rational points
194	
195	`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` states `Pic⁰_{C/k}` smooth,
196	proper and geometrically irreducible under the hypotheses
197	`[GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C]
198	[PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C]`, whereas the Albanese curve `C`
199	enters here carrying only `[SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
200	[GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]` over an algebraically closed field `k̄`. The
201	three bridging facts below discharge the missing hypotheses, so that
202	`Pic0.bundle` can be assembled from the upstream declarations. -/
203	
204	/-- **Reducedness descends along a faithfully flat morphism.** If `π : Y ⟶ X` is
205	flat and surjective (i.e. faithfully flat) and `Y` is reduced, then `X` is
206	reduced: each stalk map `𝒪_{X,π(y)} → 𝒪_{Y,y}` is a flat local homomorphism of
207	local rings, hence faithfully flat and in particular injective, so `𝒪_{X,π(y)}`
208	embeds into the reduced ring `𝒪_{Y,y}`. -/
209	theorem isReduced_of_flat_of_surjective {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (π : Y ⟶ X)
210	    [Flat π] [Surjective π] [IsReduced Y] : IsReduced X := by
211	  haveI hst : ∀ x : X, _root_.IsReduced (X.presheaf.stalk x) := by
212	    intro x
213	    obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := π.surjective x
214	    have hlocal : IsLocalHom (π.stalkMap y).hom := inferInstance
215	    have hflat : (π.stalkMap y).hom.Flat := Flat.stalkMap π y
216	    have hinj : Function.Injective (π.stalkMap y).hom := by
217	      algebraize [(π.stalkMap y).hom]
218	      haveI : Module.Flat (X.presheaf.stalk (π.base y)) (Y.presheaf.stalk y) := hflat
219	      haveI : IsLocalHom (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk (π.base y)) (Y.presheaf.stalk y)) := hlocal
220	      haveI : Module.FaithfullyFlat (X.presheaf.stalk (π.base y)) (Y.presheaf.stalk y) :=
221	        Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_flat_of_isLocalHom
222	      exact FaithfulSMul.algebraMap_injective _ _
223	    exact isReduced_of_injective (π.stalkMap y).hom hinj
224	  exact isReduced_of_isReduced_stalk X
225	
226	/-- **A scheme smooth over an algebraically closed field is geometrically
227	reduced.** For each test field `K/k̄`, the base change `X ×_{k̄} K` is smooth
228	over `K`; its further base change to `K̄ = AlgebraicClosure K` is smooth over an
229	algebraically closed field, hence reduced
230	(`Scheme.isReduced_of_smooth_of_isAlgClosed`), and reducedness descends along the
231	faithfully flat projection `X_{K̄} → X_K` (`isReduced_of_flat_of_surjective`). -/
232	theorem geometricallyReduced_of_smooth {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar] [IsAlgClosed kbar]
233	    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of kbar)) [Smooth f] :
234	    GeometricallyReduced f := by
235	  refine ⟨?_⟩
236	  rw [geometrically_iff_of_commRing_of_isClosedUnderIsomorphisms]
237	  intro K _ _
238	  have hfsurj : (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K))).hom.FaithfullyFlat :=
239	    RingHom.faithfullyFlat_algebraMap_iff.mpr inferInstance
240	  have hFS := (flat_and_surjective_SpecMap_iff
241	    (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)))).mpr hfsurj
242	  haveI : Flat (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)))) := hFS.1
243	  haveI : Surjective (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)))) := hFS.2
244	  haveI hsm1 : Smooth (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap kbar K)))) :=
245	    inferInstance
246	  haveI hsm2 : Smooth (pullback.snd
247	      (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap kbar K))))
248	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K))))) := inferInstance
249	  haveI : Smooth (Over.mk (pullback.snd
250	      (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap kbar K))))
251	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)))))).hom := hsm2
252	  haveI : IsReduced (pullback (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap kbar K))))
253	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K))))) :=
254	    Scheme.isReduced_of_smooth_of_isAlgClosed (kbar := AlgebraicClosure K) (Over.mk (pullback.snd
255	      (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap kbar K))))
256	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K))))))
257	  exact isReduced_of_flat_of_surjective
258	    (pullback.fst (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap kbar K))))
259	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)))))
260	
261	/-- **A smooth, geometrically irreducible curve over an algebraically closed
262	field has a rational point.** `C.left` is nonempty (geometric irreducibility over
263	the one-point base `Spec k̄`), locally of finite type over `k̄` (smoothness) and
264	therefore a Jacobson space, so it has a closed point `x`; over the algebraically
265	closed field `k̄`, `pointOfClosedPoint`/`pointEquivClosedPoint` promote `x` to a
266	`k̄`-rational section of `C.hom`. This discharges `[HasRationalPoint C]`. -/
267	theorem hasRationalPoint_of_isAlgClosed {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar] [IsAlgClosed kbar]
268	    (C : Over (Spec (.of kbar))) [Smooth C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
269	    Scheme.HasRationalPoint C := by
270	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom := inferInstance
271	  haveI : IrreducibleSpace C.left :=
272	    GeometricallyIrreducible.irreducibleSpace_of_subsingleton C.hom
273	  haveI : JacobsonSpace C.left := LocallyOfFiniteType.jacobsonSpace C.hom
274	  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := nonempty_inter_closedPoints (X := C.left) (Z := Set.univ)
275	    Set.univ_nonempty isClosed_univ.isLocallyClosed
276	  exact ⟨⟨(pointEquivClosedPoint C.hom).symm ⟨x, hx.2⟩⟩⟩

382	of the Abel–Jacobi morphism `ι_{P₀} : C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` at the basepoint
383	`P₀ ∈ C(k̄)`. On `k̄`-points,
384	`ι_{P₀}(Q) = [𝓞_C(Q − P₀)] ∈ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}(k̄)`; at the basepoint
385	itself `ι_{P₀}(P₀) = η_J`.

387	The morphism is the moduli classifier of
388	the rigidified diagonal correspondence
389	`𝓛^{P₀} = 𝓞_{C × C}(Δ − {P₀} × C − C × {P₀})` on `C × C`, taken as a
390	relative degree-zero line bundle on `C × C` over the second factor.

392	Blueprint reference: `lem:abel_jacobi_morphism` (Milne, *Abelian
393	Varieties*, Proposition III.6.1 and Summary III.6.11). -/

395	/-- **The Abel–Jacobi morphism at the marked basepoint `P₀`.**
396	
397	For a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve `C` over an
398	algebraically closed field `k̄` and a marked `k̄`-point
399	`P₀ : 𝟙_ ⟶ C`, the **Abel–Jacobi morphism** is the unique regular
400	morphism `ι_{P₀} : C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` characterised on `T`-points by the
401	formula `(1 × ι_{P₀})^* 𝓜^{P₀} ≈ 𝓛^{P₀}`, where `𝓜^{P₀}` is the
402	Poincaré–Picard correspondence on `C × Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` and
403	`𝓛^{P₀} = 𝓞_{C × C}(Δ − {P₀} × C − C × {P₀})`.

417	/-! ## §2. The `g`-th symmetric power `Sym^g C`
418	
419	The `g`-th symmetric power of `C` is the quotient of the `g`-fold
420	Cartesian power `C^g` by the natural permutation action of the
421	symmetric group `S_g`. Mathlib `b80f227` has no formalised symmetric
422	power of a scheme — only `Sym` / `SymmetricPower` for types and
423	modules — so the scheme-theoretic construction must be supplied
424	project-side, following Milne's recipe of §III.3 Proposition 3.1: on
425	each open affine `U = Spec A ⊆ C` form `Spec(A^{⊗ g})^{S_g}`, then glue
426	along the standard open-cover patching (Mumford 1970 §II.7 / §III.11).
427	
428	The construction is a prerequisite for the bodies of
429	`symmetricPowerAVMap` and `symmetricPowerToJacobian`, which need the
430	symmetric projection `π : C^g ⟶ Sym^g C` and its universal property. The
431	declaration below records the target `Sym^g C : Over (Spec k̄)` only; the
432	affine-and-glue construction is not yet formalised.
433	
434	Blueprint reference: `def:symmetric_power_curve` (Milne, *Abelian
435	Varieties*, §III.3, Proposition 3.1, p. 94). -/
436	
437	/-- **The `g`-th symmetric power `Sym^g C`** of a complete nonsingular
438	curve `C` over an algebraically closed field `k̄`, as a `k̄`-scheme.
439	
440	Milne III.3 Proposition 3.1 constructs `Sym^g C` as the quotient of
441	`C^g` by the natural permutation action of the symmetric group `S_g`:

640	/-! ## §6. The Albanese universal property — headline theorem
641	
642	The headline result of the chapter: for every pointed morphism
643	`φ : C ⟶ A` into an abelian variety `A` with `φ(P₀) = η_A`, there
644	exists a unique regular morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A` such that
645	`φ = ψ ∘ ι_{P₀}`. The proof follows Milne Proposition III.6.1
646	verbatim, using the four sub-lemmas above plus Milne Theorem I.3.2
647	(`extend_to_av`) and Corollary I.1.2 (a `thm:rigidity_lemma`
648	consequence).
649	
650	Blueprint reference: `thm:albanese_universal_property` (Milne,
651	*Abelian Varieties*, Proposition III.6.1, p. 104). -/
652	
653	/-- **Albanese universal property of `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` — Milne III §6
654	Proposition 6.1.**
655	
656	For a complete nonsingular curve `C` of genus `g > 0` over an
657	algebraically closed field `k̄`, a marked `k̄`-point `P₀ ∈ C(k̄)`, and
658	every pointed morphism `φ : C ⟶ A` into an abelian variety `A` with
659	`φ(P₀) = η_A`, there exists a *unique* regular morphism
660	`ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A` such that `φ = ι_{P₀} ≫ ψ`.
661	
662	Proof sketch (Milne III.6.1):
663	1. **Symmetrisation.** `(P₁,…,P_g) ↦ φ(P₁) + ⋯ + φ(P_g)` is
664	   `S_g`-symmetric (`A` commutative), so factors through
665	   `Sym^g C` as `Sym^g φ` (`lem:symmetric_product_av_map`).
666	2. **Descent to a regular morphism on `J`.** The birational morphism
667	   `f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` (`lem:symmetric_product_to_jacobian`)
668	   exhibits `Sym^g φ ∘ (f^{(g)})^{-1}` as a rational map
669	   `Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⇢ A`, which by Milne Theorem I.3.2 extends uniquely to
670	   a regular morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`
671	   (`lem:descent_through_birational_sigma`).
672	3. **Factorisation `ψ ∘ ι_{P₀} = φ`.** Use Milne's identification of
673	   `ι_{P₀}` with the composite `Q ↦ Q + (g − 1) P₀` followed by
674	   `f^{(g)}`; together with `φ(P₀) = η_A` and the additive structure
675	   of `A`, this gives `ψ(ι_{P₀}(Q)) = φ(Q)` on `k̄`-points, hence
676	   globally by the reduced-and-separated agreement principle.
677	4. **Homomorphism property.** `ψ` sends `η_J = ι_{P₀}(P₀)` to
678	   `φ(P₀) = η_A`, so by Milne Corollary I.1.2 (a `thm:rigidity_lemma`
679	   consequence) it is a homomorphism of group schemes.
680	5. **Uniqueness.** Two homomorphisms `Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A` with the same
681	   restriction to `ι_{P₀}(C)` agree on the `g`-fold sum
682	   `ι_{P₀}(C) + ⋯ + ι_{P₀}(C) = Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` (since `f^{(g)}` is
683	   surjective), hence are equal.
684	
685	The statement asserts only the existence and uniqueness of the factoring
686	morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A` (matching the project's `IsAlbanese`
687	convention in `Jacobian.lean`); the group-homomorphism property is implicit
688	in the construction, by Milne Corollary I.1.2 (registered in
689	`chap:AbelianVarietyRigidity`).
690	
691	The proof below is pure assembly: `descentThroughBirationalSigma` (§5)
692	transported across `albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq` (§5.5). Both of
693	those, and the constructions of §1–§4 they rest on, are still unproved —
694	see the file header.
695	
696	**Therefore this theorem is NOT sorry-free**, and must not be reported as a
697	landed result. `#print axioms albanese_universal_property` reports
698	`[propext, sorryAx, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` (measured, run 0069). The
699	assembly is honest and the statement is the right one; what is missing is
700	everything the statement quantifies over — in particular `abelJacobi`, whose
701	`sorry`-bodied *definition* means the equation `φ = abelJacobi C P₀ ≫ ψ` does
702	not yet say what it is meant to say. Step 4 (the homomorphism property, via
703	Milne Corollary I.1.2) does have a real input: the rigidity chain in
704	`RigidityLemma.lean` is sorry-free and axiom-clean. -/
705	theorem albanese_universal_property
706	    (_hg : 0 < genus C)
707	    (P0 : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of kbar))) ⟶ C)
708	    {A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
709	    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]
710	    (φ : C ⟶ A) (_hφ : P0 ≫ φ = η[A]) :
711	    ∃! (ψ : jacobianScheme C ⟶ A), φ = abelJacobi C P0 ≫ ψ := by
712	  -- Transport the symmetric-power descent `descentThroughBirationalSigma`
713	  -- across the connecting biconditional `albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq`.
714	  have key := albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq C P0 φ _hφ
715	  obtain ⟨ψ, hψ_sym, huniq_sym⟩ := descentThroughBirationalSigma C P0 φ _hφ
716	  exact ⟨ψ, (key ψ).mpr hψ_sym,
717	    fun ψ' hψ' => huniq_sym ψ' ((key ψ').mp hψ')⟩
718

12	/-!
13	# The Albanese universal property, proved over the symmetric-power interface
14	
15	`Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean` pins Milne's Proposition III.6.1 in the shape the
16	challenge wants, but its six obligations are stated against `Pic0.SymmetricPower`,
17	a `sorry`-bodied definition. An equation between morphisms out of a junk term
18	carries no information, so those obligations cannot be discharged — and should not
19	be, since discharging them would prove nothing.
20	
21	This file does the mathematics instead. It takes the symmetric power as the
22	**interface** `SymPowData` (`Albanese/SymPowInterface.lean`), which is inhabited
23	(`symPowDataOne`), and proves Milne's argument over it with no `sorry` and no
24	appeal to an unproved statement. What the challenge still owes is then exactly one
25	thing — `SymPowData C g` for `g ≥ 2`, the missing scheme quotient — rather than six
26	entangled gaps.
27	
28	## The two directions of the connector, and why each is now real
29	
30	Milne's proof turns the Albanese equation `φ = aj ≫ ψ` into the symmetric-power
31	equation `Sym^g φ = f^{(g)} ≫ ψ`. Both directions are proved here:
32	
33	* **Forward** (`symAVMap_eq_of_albanese_eq`). Assume `φ = aj ≫ ψ` where the
34	  Abel–Jacobi map is realised, as Milne realises it, through the basepoint shift:
35	  `aj = basePointShift P₀ i₀ ≫ proj ≫ f`. Then `Sym^g φ` and `f ≫ ψ` agree after
36	  `proj`, because pushing `ψ` through the `g`-fold sum is
37	  `map_prod (IsMonHom.monoidHom ψ _)` — this is where `ψ` being a *homomorphism*
38	  is used, and it is exactly Milne's step 5. Uniqueness in the interface then
39	  gives the equation on the carrier.
40	* **Backward** (`albanese_eq_of_symAVMap_eq`). Restrict along
41	  `Q ↦ (Q, P₀, …, P₀)` and collapse: `MonObj.basePointShift_comp_powSum`
42	  (proved in `SymPowInterface.lean`) says the `g`-fold sum of a *pointed* `φ` over
43	  that tuple is `φ` itself. No quotient property is needed for this direction at
44	  all — only the interface's defining equation.
45	
46	## Main results
47	
48	* `albaneseFactorisation_iff` — the connecting biconditional
49	  `(φ = aj ≫ ψ) ↔ (Sym^g φ = f ≫ ψ)`, over the interface. This is the honest form
50	  of `Pic0.albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq`.
51	* `exists_unique_albanese_factorisation` — **the Albanese universal property**:
52	  given the interface, the birational descent datum, and pointed rigidity, there is
53	  a unique `ψ` with `φ = aj ≫ ψ`. Milne Proposition III.6.1.
54	* `exists_unique_descent_of_section` (§2) — the descent datum supplied from its
55	  geometric source: a morphism on a dense open of the Jacobian. This is where
56	  `extend_to_av` (Milne I.3.2, proved and unconditional) does its work, and it is
57	  the form the eventual `Sym^g C` construction would feed.
58	* `exists_unique_descent_of_birational` (§2) — **Milne's step 2 in full.** The descent
59	  datum `hdesc` above, produced from exactly what Milne III.5.1(a) gives: a section of
60	  `f^{(g)}` over a dense open `V`, a matching retraction, and density of `V` and of
61	  `f⁻¹V`. Its conclusion `∃! ψ, h = f ≫ ψ` is an equation on *all* of `Sym^g C`, not
62	  merely on `V`, which is what the connector consumes.
63	* `exists_unique_descent_over` (§2) — the same datum transported from underlying
64	  scheme morphisms into `Over (Spec k̄)`, which is where the connector lives. The
65	  structure-map compatibility is **not** an extra hypothesis: it follows from
66	  dominance of `f` (`comp_hom_of_descent_eq`).
67	* `hom_ext_of_dense_open` — the agreement principle used for uniqueness.
68	
69	## What remains, precisely
70	
71	Only `SymPowData C g` for the actual curve and `g = genus C`, together with Milne
72	III.5.1(a) birationality in the concrete form `exists_unique_descent_of_birational`
73	consumes (section + retraction + two density facts). Everything Milne derives *from*
74	those is proved below — including, note, the step that used to be described as blocked
75	on "a way to invert a birational morphism": no birational-inverse API is needed, only
76	the section and retraction that birationality supplies directly.

106	/-! ### The hypotheses on `f^{(g)}`, and why they are the right two
107	
108	Milne's cycle map is *defined* as the symmetrisation of the Abel–Jacobi map:
109	`f^{(g)} ∘ π = aj(P₁) + ⋯ + aj(P_g)`. That single equation (`hf` below) is the only
110	property of `f^{(g)}` the argument uses, and when `f = D.symAVMap aj` it holds by
111	`proj_comp_symAVMap`. The second hypothesis is Milne's basepoint condition
112	`aj(P₀) = η_J`, part of `lem:abel_jacobi_morphism`.
113	
114	Together they *imply* Milne's identification of `aj` with `Q ↦ Q + (g−1) P₀`
115	followed by `f^{(g)}` — see `basePointShift_proj_comp`, which is
116	`basePointShift_comp_powSum` applied to `aj` itself. So that identification is
117	derived here, not assumed. -/
118	
119	/-- **Milne's identification of the Abel–Jacobi map, derived.** If `f^{(g)}` is the
120	symmetrisation of a *pointed* `aj`, then `Q ↦ Q + (g−1) P₀` followed by `f^{(g)}`
121	is `aj`.
122	
123	This is `basePointShift_comp_powSum` applied to `aj`: the `g`-fold sum of `aj` over
124	`(Q, P₀, …, P₀)` collapses to `aj(Q)` because `aj(P₀) = η_J`. -/
125	theorem basePointShift_proj_comp [MonObj J] [IsCommMonObj J]
126	    (D : SymPowData C g) (f : D.carrier ⟶ J) (P0 : 𝟙_ K ⟶ C) (i₀ : Fin g)
127	    (aj : C ⟶ J) (hf : D.proj ≫ f = powSum g aj) (haj0 : P0 ≫ aj = η[J]) :
128	    basePointShift P0 i₀ ≫ D.proj ≫ f = aj := by
129	  rw [hf]
130	  exact basePointShift_comp_powSum P0 i₀ aj haj0
131	
132	/-- **Forward direction.** If `φ` factors through the Abel–Jacobi map, then
133	`Sym^g φ` factors through `f^{(g)}` with the same `ψ`.
134	
135	The proof compares both sides after `proj`. On the left the interface's defining
136	equation gives the `g`-fold sum of `φ`; on the right `hf` gives the `g`-fold sum of
137	`aj`, then postcomposed with `ψ`. These agree because `ψ`, being a **homomorphism**
138	of monoid objects, commutes with a finite product in the hom-monoid
139	(`map_prod (IsMonHom.monoidHom ψ _)`) — this is where Milne's step 5 uses that `ψ`
140	is a homomorphism and not merely a morphism. Uniqueness through `proj` then upgrades
141	the agreement to the carrier. -/
142	theorem symAVMap_eq_of_albanese_eq
143	    [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A] [MonObj J] [IsCommMonObj J]
144	    (D : SymPowData C g) (f : D.carrier ⟶ J)
145	    (hproj : ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin g), MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj)
146	    (aj : C ⟶ J) (hf : D.proj ≫ f = powSum g aj)
147	    (φ : C ⟶ A) (ψ : J ⟶ A) [IsMonHom ψ] (hφ : φ = aj ≫ ψ) :
148	    D.symAVMap φ = f ≫ ψ := by
149	  classical
150	  refine (D.hom_ext_of_proj hproj ?_).symm
151	  rw [D.proj_comp_symAVMap, ← Category.assoc, hf]
152	  -- `ψ` is a monoid-object homomorphism, so it commutes with the `g`-fold sum.
153	  rw [show (powSum g aj ≫ ψ) = ∏ i, ((Pi.π (fun _ : Fin g => C) i ≫ aj) ≫ ψ) from
154	    map_prod (IsMonHom.monoidHom ψ _) _ Finset.univ]
155	  rw [powSum]
156	  exact Finset.prod_congr rfl fun i _ => by rw [Category.assoc, ← hφ]
157	
158	/-- **Backward direction.** If `Sym^g φ` factors through `f^{(g)}`, then `φ` factors
159	through the Abel–Jacobi map — provided `φ` is *pointed* (`P₀ ≫ φ = η[A]`).
160	
161	This direction needs neither the quotient property nor that `ψ` is a homomorphism:
162	restrict the given equation along the basepoint shift `Q ↦ (Q, P₀, …, P₀)` and the
163	left side collapses to `φ` by `basePointShift_comp_powSum`, while the right side
164	becomes `aj ≫ ψ` by `basePointShift_proj_comp`. That is the whole force of Milne's
165	"restrict along `Q ↦ Q + (g−1) P₀` and use `φ(P₀) = η_A`". -/
166	theorem albanese_eq_of_symAVMap_eq
167	    [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A] [MonObj J] [IsCommMonObj J]
168	    (D : SymPowData C g) (f : D.carrier ⟶ J) (P0 : 𝟙_ K ⟶ C) (i₀ : Fin g)
169	    (aj : C ⟶ J) (hf : D.proj ≫ f = powSum g aj) (haj0 : P0 ≫ aj = η[J])
170	    (φ : C ⟶ A) (hφ : P0 ≫ φ = η[A]) (ψ : J ⟶ A)
171	    (h : D.symAVMap φ = f ≫ ψ) :
172	    φ = aj ≫ ψ := by
173	  have key : basePointShift P0 i₀ ≫ D.proj ≫ D.symAVMap φ
174	      = basePointShift P0 i₀ ≫ D.proj ≫ (f ≫ ψ) := by rw [h]
175	  rw [D.proj_comp_symAVMap, basePointShift_comp_powSum P0 i₀ φ hφ] at key
176	  rw [key, ← Category.assoc D.proj f ψ, ← Category.assoc,
177	    basePointShift_proj_comp D f P0 i₀ aj hf haj0]
178	
179	/-- **The connecting biconditional (Milne's identification).** Over the symmetric-power
180	interface, the Albanese-form factorisation and the symmetric-power-form factorisation
181	of a pointed `φ` through a *homomorphism* `ψ` are equivalent.
182	
183	This is the honest content of `Pic0.albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq`: same
184	mathematics, but stated about a symmetric power that is named rather than `sorry`ed,
185	so the equation says what it is meant to say. -/
186	theorem albaneseFactorisation_iff
187	    [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A] [MonObj J] [IsCommMonObj J]
188	    (D : SymPowData C g) (f : D.carrier ⟶ J) (P0 : 𝟙_ K ⟶ C) (i₀ : Fin g)
189	    (hproj : ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin g), MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj)
190	    (aj : C ⟶ J) (hf : D.proj ≫ f = powSum g aj) (haj0 : P0 ≫ aj = η[J])
191	    (φ : C ⟶ A) (hφ : P0 ≫ φ = η[A]) (ψ : J ⟶ A) [IsMonHom ψ] :
192	    (φ = aj ≫ ψ) ↔ (D.symAVMap φ = f ≫ ψ) :=
193	  ⟨fun h => symAVMap_eq_of_albanese_eq D f hproj aj hf φ ψ h,
194	   fun h => albanese_eq_of_symAVMap_eq D f P0 i₀ aj hf haj0 φ hφ ψ h⟩
195	
196	/-- **The Albanese universal property over the interface — Milne Proposition III.6.1.**
197	
198	Given
199	* the symmetric-power interface `D` with symmetric projection `proj`,
200	* the cycle map `f = f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ J` presented as the symmetrisation of a
201	  pointed Abel–Jacobi map `aj` (`hf`, `haj0`),
202	* **pointed rigidity** (`hom`): every *pointed* morphism `J ⟶ A` is a homomorphism —
203	  Milne Corollary I.1.2, which for schemes is
204	  `AlgebraicGeometry.av_regularMap_isHom_of_zero` (proved, `RigidityLemma.lean`),
205	* the **descent datum** (`hdesc`): a unique `ψ` with `Sym^g φ = f ≫ ψ`,
206	
207	there is a unique `ψ` with `φ = aj ≫ ψ`.
208	
209	The proof is Milne's, transported across `albaneseFactorisation_iff`. Note that
210	`hom` is applied only after checking that the candidate `ψ` really is pointed, which
211	is itself derived: `η[J] = aj(P₀)` by `haj0`, so `η[J] ≫ ψ = φ(P₀) = η[A]`. Nothing
212	here rests on a `sorry`-bodied object; the descent datum is Milne's step 2 and is
213	supplied geometrically by `exists_unique_descent_of_section` in §2. -/
214	theorem exists_unique_albanese_factorisation
215	    [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A] [MonObj J] [IsCommMonObj J]
216	    (D : SymPowData C g) (f : D.carrier ⟶ J) (P0 : 𝟙_ K ⟶ C) (i₀ : Fin g)
217	    (hproj : ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin g), MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj)
218	    (aj : C ⟶ J) (hf : D.proj ≫ f = powSum g aj) (haj0 : P0 ≫ aj = η[J])
219	    (φ : C ⟶ A) (hφ : P0 ≫ φ = η[A])
220	    (hom : ∀ ψ : J ⟶ A, η[J] ≫ ψ = η[A] → IsMonHom ψ)
221	    (hdesc : ∃! ψ : J ⟶ A, D.symAVMap φ = f ≫ ψ) :
222	    ∃! ψ : J ⟶ A, φ = aj ≫ ψ := by
223	  -- A `ψ` satisfying either factorisation is automatically pointed: `η[J] = aj(P₀)`.
224	  have hpt : ∀ ψ : J ⟶ A, φ = aj ≫ ψ → η[J] ≫ ψ = η[A] := by
225	    intro ψ hψ
226	    rw [← haj0, Category.assoc, ← hψ, hφ]
227	  obtain ⟨ψ, hψ, huniq⟩ := hdesc
228	  -- The witness is pointed *before* we may call rigidity, so establish that first
229	  -- from the symmetric-power side, via the backward direction.
230	  have hψalb : φ = aj ≫ ψ :=
231	    albanese_eq_of_symAVMap_eq D f P0 i₀ aj hf haj0 φ hφ ψ hψ
232	  refine ⟨ψ, hψalb, ?_⟩
233	  intro ψ' hψ'
234	  haveI := hom ψ' (hpt ψ' hψ')
235	  exact huniq ψ'
236	    ((albaneseFactorisation_iff D f P0 i₀ hproj aj hf haj0 φ hφ ψ').mp hψ')
237	
238	end Connector

240	end CategoryTheory

242	/-! ## §2. Supplying the descent datum geometrically
243	
244	At schemes over an algebraically closed field the descent datum of §1 is not an
245	assumption: it follows from a section of `f^{(g)}` over a dense open of the Jacobian,
246	by the rational-map extension `extend_to_av` (Milne I.3.2, proved and unconditional)
247	packaged as `exists_unique_hom_restrict_eq_of_dense_open`. -/
248	
249	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
250	
251	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj
252	
253	variable {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar] [IsAlgClosed kbar]
254	
255	/-- **Milne's descent step, from birationality data.**
256	
257	Let `J` be an abelian variety over `k̄`, let `V ⊆ J` be a **dense open**, and let
258	`s : V ⟶ Sym^g C` be a section of `f^{(g)}` over `V` (i.e. `s ≫ f = V.ι`, which is
259	what birationality of `f^{(g)}` provides — Milne III.5.1(a)). Then for any
260	`h : Sym^g C ⟶ A` there is a unique `ψ : J ⟶ A` with `V.ι ≫ ψ = s ≫ h`.
261	
262	Existence and uniqueness are `exists_unique_hom_restrict_eq_of_dense_open`, i.e.
263	Milne Theorem I.3.2; the section is the only new input. This is the *only* step of
264	the Albanese proof that uses the rational-map extension, and its input is now
265	completely explicit. -/
266	theorem exists_unique_descent_of_section
267	    {J : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
268	    [Smooth J.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] [IsSeparated J.hom]
269	    [LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom] [IsIntegral J.left] [IsReduced J.left]
270	    {A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
271	    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]
272	    (V : J.left.Opens) (hV : Dense (V : Set J.left)) (k : (V : Scheme) ⟶ A.left)
273	    (hover : (Scheme.PartialMap.mk V hV k).toRationalMap.compHom A.hom
274	      = J.hom.toRationalMap) :
275	    ∃! ψ : J.left ⟶ A.left, V.ι ≫ ψ = k :=
276	  Scheme.RationalMap.exists_unique_hom_restrict_eq_of_dense_open V hV k hover
277	
278	/-- **A dense open inclusion is dominant.** Used to transport an equation proved on a
279	dense open to the whole (reduced) scheme. -/
280	theorem isDominant_opens_ι {X : Scheme.{u}} (V : X.Opens) (hV : Dense (V : Set X)) :
281	    IsDominant V.ι := by
282	  rw [isDominant_iff]
283	  simpa [DenseRange, Scheme.Opens.range_ι] using hV
284	
285	/-- **Milne's step 2 in full, from birationality data.**
286	
287	This is the descent datum `hdesc` of `exists_unique_albanese_factorisation`, produced
288	from exactly what Milne III.5.1(a) provides. Suppose `f : S ⟶ J` (morally
289	`f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰`) is an **isomorphism over a dense open** `V ⊆ J`, presented
290	concretely as
291	
292	* `s : V ⟶ S` with `s ≫ f = V.ι` — a section of `f` over `V`;
293	* `hsr` — and `s` is also a retraction of the restriction `f|_{f⁻¹V} : f⁻¹V ⟶ V`;
294	* `hVpre` — the preimage `f⁻¹V` is dense in `S`.
295	
296	Then for any `h : S ⟶ A` into an abelian variety there is a **unique** `ψ : J ⟶ A`
297	with `h = f ≫ ψ`.
298	
299	Note the shape of the conclusion: the equation is on **all** of `S`, not merely on
300	`V`. That is the difference between this and
301	`exists_unique_hom_restrict_eq_of_dense_open`, and it is where `hsr` and `hVpre` earn
302	their place — the extension theorem gives the equation on `V`, and agreement is then
303	transported to all of `S` along the dense open `f⁻¹V` (`ext_of_isDominant`, using that
304	`S` is reduced and `A` separated).
305	
306	So the Albanese descent needs no birational-inverse API. The full call-site bill is
307	**five** items, not four: the section `s`, the retraction `hsr`, the two density facts
308	`hV` and `hVpre`, and `hover` — the compatibility of the partial map with the structure
309	morphisms over `k̄`, which is what `exists_unique_hom_restrict_eq_of_dense_open`
310	(`Albanese/DenseOpenDescent.lean`) consumes. `hover` is a genuine hypothesis; it is
311	listed here because an earlier draft of this docstring omitted it. -/
312	theorem exists_unique_descent_of_birational
313	    {S J : Over (Spec (.of kbar))} [IsReduced S.left]
314	    [Smooth J.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] [IsSeparated J.hom]
315	    [LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom] [IsIntegral J.left] [IsReduced J.left]
316	    {A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
317	    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]
318	    (f : S.left ⟶ J.left) (h : S.left ⟶ A.left)
319	    (V : J.left.Opens) (hV : Dense (V : Set J.left))
320	    (hVpre : Dense ((f ⁻¹ᵁ V : S.left.Opens) : Set S.left))
321	    (s : (V : Scheme) ⟶ S.left) (hs : s ≫ f = V.ι)
322	    (hsr : f.resLE V (f ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl ≫ s = (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι)
323	    (hover : (Scheme.PartialMap.mk V hV (s ≫ h)).toRationalMap.compHom A.hom
324	      = J.hom.toRationalMap) :
325	    ∃! ψ : J.left ⟶ A.left, h = f ≫ ψ := by
326	  haveI : A.left.IsSeparated := Scheme.RationalMap.isSeparated_left_of_isProper A
327	  haveI hdom : IsDominant (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι := by
328	    rw [isDominant_iff]
329	    simpa [DenseRange, Scheme.Opens.range_ι] using hVpre
330	  obtain ⟨ψ, hψ, huniq⟩ :=
331	    Scheme.RationalMap.exists_unique_hom_restrict_eq_of_dense_open V hV (s ≫ h) hover
332	  refine ⟨ψ, ?_, ?_⟩
333	  · -- Both sides agree on the dense open `f⁻¹(V)`; transport to all of `S`.
334	    refine ext_of_isDominant (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι ?_
335	    calc (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι ≫ h
336	        = (f.resLE V (f ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl ≫ s) ≫ h := by rw [hsr]
337	      _ = f.resLE V (f ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl ≫ (s ≫ h) := by simp
338	      _ = f.resLE V (f ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl ≫ (V.ι ≫ ψ) := by rw [hψ]
339	      _ = (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι ≫ f ≫ ψ := by
340	            rw [← Category.assoc,
341	              show f.resLE V (f ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl ≫ V.ι = (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι ≫ f from by
342	                simp [Scheme.Hom.resLE], Category.assoc]
343	  · intro ψ' hψ'
344	    refine huniq ψ' ?_
345	    change V.ι ≫ ψ' = s ≫ h
346	    rw [← hs, Category.assoc, ← hψ']
347	
348	/-! ### Crossing from scheme morphisms to `Over (Spec k̄)` morphisms
349	
350	`exists_unique_descent_of_birational` concludes about `J.left ⟶ A.left`, whereas the
351	connector of §1 lives in `Over (Spec k̄)`. The two lemmas below cross that gap, and the
352	crossing is free rather than an extra hypothesis: compatibility with the structure
353	morphisms is *automatic* once `f` is dominant. -/
354	
355	omit [IsAlgClosed kbar] in
356	/-- **Compatibility over `k̄` is automatic.** If `f : S ⟶ J` has dominant underlying
357	morphism and `ψ` satisfies `h.left = f.left ≫ ψ`, then `ψ` is a morphism over `k̄`:
358	`ψ ≫ A.hom = J.hom`.
359	
360	Both sides agree after the dominant `f.left` (each reduces to the structure morphism of
361	`S`, by `h.w` and `f.w`), and `J.left` is reduced, so `ext_of_isDominant` concludes.
362	This is why the descent produces an honest `Over` morphism without assuming it. -/
363	theorem comp_hom_of_descent_eq
364	    {S J A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))} [IsReduced J.left]
365	    (f : S ⟶ J) (h : S ⟶ A) (ψ : J.left ⟶ A.left)
366	    (hfd : IsDominant f.left) (hψ : h.left = f.left ≫ ψ) :
367	    ψ ≫ A.hom = J.hom := by
368	  refine ext_of_isDominant f.left ?_
369	  rw [← Category.assoc, ← hψ]
370	  exact h.w.trans f.w.symm
371	
372	omit [IsAlgClosed kbar] in
373	/-- **Transport the descent datum into `Over (Spec k̄)`.** A unique factorisation of
374	underlying scheme morphisms upgrades to a unique factorisation of `k̄`-morphisms, using
375	`comp_hom_of_descent_eq` for the structure-map compatibility.
376	
377	This delivers `hdesc` in exactly the shape `exists_unique_albanese_factorisation`
378	consumes. -/
379	theorem exists_unique_descent_over
380	    {S J A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))} [IsReduced J.left]
381	    (f : S ⟶ J) (h : S ⟶ A) (hfd : IsDominant f.left)
382	    (hyp : ∃! ψ : J.left ⟶ A.left, h.left = f.left ≫ ψ) :
383	    ∃! ψ : J ⟶ A, h = f ≫ ψ := by
384	  obtain ⟨ψ, hψ, huniq⟩ := hyp
385	  refine ⟨Over.homMk ψ (comp_hom_of_descent_eq f h ψ hfd hψ),
386	    Over.OverMorphism.ext (by simpa using hψ), ?_⟩
387	  intro ψ' hψ'
388	  refine Over.OverMorphism.ext ?_
389	  exact huniq ψ'.left (by simpa using congrArg Over.Hom.left (a₁ := h) hψ')
390	
391	omit [IsAlgClosed kbar] in
392	/-- **Uniqueness of the Albanese descent, geometrically.** Two morphisms from the
393	Jacobian to an abelian variety that agree on a dense open are equal — the
394	reduced-and-separated agreement principle, in the form the descent uses. -/
395	theorem hom_ext_of_dense_open
396	    {J : Over (Spec (.of kbar))} [IsReduced J.left]
397	    {A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))} [IsProper A.hom]
398	    (V : J.left.Opens) (hV : Dense (V : Set J.left))
399	    {ψ₁ ψ₂ : J.left ⟶ A.left} (h : V.ι ≫ ψ₁ = V.ι ≫ ψ₂) : ψ₁ = ψ₂ := by
400	  haveI : A.left.IsSeparated := Scheme.RationalMap.isSeparated_left_of_isProper A
401	  haveI := isDominant_opens_ι V hV
402	  exact ext_of_isDominant V.ι h

404	/-! ## §3. End to end: `SymPowData` + birationality ⟹ the Albanese universal property
405	
406	The capstone. Everything above is assembled into one statement whose hypotheses are
407	**only** the two things this leg genuinely owes:
408	
409	1. `D : SymPowData C g` — the symmetric power with its universal property;
410	2. Milne III.5.1(a) birationality of `f^{(g)}`, in the concrete form of a section `s`
411	   over a dense open `V`, a matching retraction, dominance, and two density facts.
412	
413	No `sorry`-bodied object appears, no rational-map reasoning is left at the call site,
414	and the result is axiom-clean.
415	
416	**Stated precisely, so "finished" is not read too generously.** What is proved is the
417	*implication*: given (1) and (2), Milne III.6.1 holds. Every step of his argument is
418	machine-checked, and no step of it is what remains. But the antecedent is currently
419	witnessed only for `g = 1` (`symPowDataOne` with `symPowDataOne_proj_perm`), which is
420	the case where the group-law step degenerates — see the warning in
421	`Albanese/SymPowInterface.lean`. So this is a complete argument awaiting a
422	construction, not a theorem about the actual `Sym^g C`. -/
423	
424	/-- **Milne Proposition III.6.1, end to end.**
425	
426	From the symmetric-power interface and Milne III.5.1(a)'s birationality data alone, a
427	pointed `φ : C ⟶ A` into an abelian variety factors uniquely through the pointed
428	`aj : C ⟶ J` whose symmetrisation is `f`:
429	
430	`∃! ψ : J ⟶ A, φ = aj ≫ ψ`.
431	
432	**Axiom-clean** (`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`). The chain is
433	`exists_unique_descent_of_birational` → `exists_unique_descent_over` →
434	`exists_unique_albanese_factorisation`, with commutativity and pointed rigidity
435	supplied by `Albanese/AVSelfProduct.lean`.
436	
437	Note that no curve hypothesis appears: `g` is just the number of factors. -/
438	theorem exists_unique_albanese_factorisation_of_birational
439	    {C : Over (Spec (.of kbar))} {g : ℕ}
440	    (D : SymPowData C g)
441	    (hproj : ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin g), permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj)
442	    (P0 : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of kbar))) ⟶ C) (i₀ : Fin g)
443	    {J A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
444	    [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom]
445	    [IsIntegral J.left] [IsReduced J.left]
446	    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]
447	    [IsReduced (D.carrier).left]
448	    (φ : C ⟶ A) (hφ : P0 ≫ φ = η[A])
449	    (aj : C ⟶ J) (f : D.carrier ⟶ J)
450	    (hf : letI : IsCommMonObj J := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package J
451	      D.proj ≫ f = powSum g aj)
452	    (haj0 : P0 ≫ aj = η[J])
453	    (hfd : IsDominant f.left)
454	    (V : J.left.Opens) (hV : Dense (V : Set J.left))
